explanation: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) won 209 of 300 seats in the general election (results: February 18, 2026), routing rivals. The Awami League had been banned. The election ended the post-Hasina interim period led by Muhammad Yunus.

question_text: Who was sworn in as Prime Minister of Bangladesh on February 17, 2026, following the BNP's election victory?
explanation: Tarek Rahman (Tarique Rahman), son of Khaleda Zia and acting BNP chairman, was sworn in as Bangladesh's Prime Minister on February 17, 2026, by President Mohammed Shahabuddin, after the BNP won 209/300 seats. The Awami League had been banned.

question_text: Which major political party was banned in Bangladesh ahead of the February 2026 general elections?
explanation: The Awami League (founded by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman) was banned in Bangladesh ahead of the February 2026 general elections, paving the way for the BNP's 209/300 seat victory and the swearing-in of Tarek Rahman as PM on February 17, 2026.

question_text: Following the LDP's mid-term victory on February 8, 2026, who became Japan's first-ever female Prime Minister?
explanation: Sanae Takaichi (LDP) became Japan's first-ever female Prime Minister after the LDP won 316/465 seats in the February 8, 2026 mid-term election. Takaichi, a conservative protégé of late PM Shinzo Abe, broke a 70-year glass ceiling in Japanese politics.

question_text: In Japan's mid-term election on February 8, 2026, how many of the 465 lower-house seats did the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) win?
explanation: The Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) won 316 of 465 seats in Japan's lower house mid-term election on February 8, 2026, giving it a two-thirds supermajority. Sanae Takaichi was then sworn in as Japan's first female Prime Minister.

question_text: Around February 2026, tensions rose between Moldova and the breakaway Transnistria region. Who is the President of Moldova?
explanation: Maia Sandu is the President of Moldova. In February 2026, tensions with the breakaway Transnistria region (PMR) spiked, with approximately 1,500 Russian troops stationed there. Sandu's pro-EU government has pushed for closer Western integration.

question_text: Which NATO exercises launched on February 11, 2026, focus on securing the High North and Arctic region?
explanation: NATO launched exercises 'Arctic Sentry' and 'Arctic Endurance' on February 11, 2026, to bolster security in the High North/Arctic region amid Russian and Chinese activity. The exercises follow Finland's (2023) and Sweden's (2024) accession to NATO.

question_text: In February 2026, Israel demolished the United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA) headquarters located in which East Jerusalem neighbourhood?
explanation: Israel demolished the UNRWA headquarters in Sheikh Jarrah, East Jerusalem, in February 2026, drawing international condemnation. UNRWA, founded in 1949, has been the primary aid agency for Palestinian refugees; Israel had outlawed its operations in late 2024.

question_text: On February 3, 2026, Japan restarted Kashiwazaki-Kariwa, which holds what distinction?
explanation: Kashiwazaki-Kariwa in Niigata Prefecture is the world's largest nuclear power plant by net capacity (~7,965 MW, 7 reactors). Japan restarted it on February 3, 2026 — the country's first nuclear plant restart since the 2011 Fukushima Daiichi disaster.

question_text: The Kashiwazaki-Kariwa restart on February 3, 2026, was significant because it was Japan's first such restart since which event?
explanation: The Kashiwazaki-Kariwa restart (Feb 3, 2026) was Japan's first nuclear plant restart since the March 11, 2011 Fukushima Daiichi disaster, which had led to a nationwide shutdown of nuclear power. Japan has been gradually reviving nuclear energy amid energy security concerns.

question_text: On January 27, 2026, France voted (180-21) to ban social media for under-15s, becoming the second country in the world to do so. Which was the first?
explanation: Australia was the first country to legislate a social-media ban for minors (under-16) in late 2024. France's National Assembly voted 180-21 on January 27, 2026, to ban social media for under-15s, becoming the second country to enact such a ban.

question_text: On January 27, 2026, which country, bucking the US/EU trend, voted to grant legal status to undocumented migrants?
explanation: Spain voted on January 27, 2026, to grant legal status to undocumented migrants — moving against the broader US and EU trend of tightening migration policy. PM Pedro Sánchez's coalition cited demographic and labour-market needs.

question_text: In February 2026, the European Union formally declared which body a terrorist organisation and sanctioned 15 of its officials?
explanation: The EU formally designated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organisation in February 2026, also sanctioning 15 IRGC officials. The move followed the December 2025 unrest in Iran and IRGC's role in regional proxy conflicts.

question_text: On January 30, 2026, South Africa expelled which Israeli diplomat?
explanation: South Africa expelled Israeli Deputy Ambassador Ariel Seidman on January 30, 2026, in protest against Israeli actions in Gaza and the demolition of the UNRWA headquarters. South Africa had earlier filed a genocide case against Israel at the ICJ (December 2023).

question_text: The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists set the 2026 Doomsday Clock to how many seconds to midnight in February 2026?
explanation: The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists set the Doomsday Clock at 85 seconds to midnight in February 2026 — the closest ever to symbolic 'midnight'. The 2025 setting was 89 seconds; the move closer cited nuclear, AI and climate risks.

question_text: On January 17, 2026, Yoweri Museveni won his seventh term as President of Uganda with what vote share?
explanation: Yoweri Museveni won a 7th term as President of Uganda on January 17, 2026, with 71.65% of the vote. Opposition leader Bobi Wine (Robert Kyagulanyi) of the NUP came second with 24.72%. Museveni has been in power since 1986.

question_text: The World Economic Forum (WEF) Annual Meeting held at Davos from January 19-23, 2026, was its which edition?
explanation: The 56th WEF Annual Meeting was held at Davos-Klosters, Switzerland, from January 19-23, 2026, with the theme 'A Spirit of Dialogue'. About 3,000 delegates including 50+ heads of state attended. The Gaza Peace Council was launched on the sidelines (Jan 22).

question_text: What was the theme of the 56th WEF Annual Meeting at Davos (January 19-23, 2026)?
explanation: 'A Spirit of Dialogue' was the theme of the 56th WEF Annual Meeting at Davos (Jan 19-23, 2026), attended by ~3,000 delegates. The 55th edition (2025) had the theme 'Collaboration for the Intelligent Age'.

question_text: The Genome Valley Excellence Award at the 23rd BioAsia at Hyderabad (Feb 17-18, 2026), themed 'TechBio Unleashed', was presented to whom?
explanation: Dr. Bruce L. Levine (University of Pennsylvania, pioneer of CAR-T cell therapy) received the Genome Valley Excellence Award at the 23rd BioAsia, held in Hyderabad on February 17-18, 2026. The theme was 'TechBio Unleashed', focusing on the convergence of biology and technology.

question_text: Which arms-control treaty between the US and Russia expired on February 5, 2026, leaving no major nuclear arms limitation regime in force between the two powers?
explanation: The New START Treaty (signed 2010, came into force 2011) expired on February 5, 2026 — leaving no bilateral nuclear arms limitation treaty between the US and Russia. The two sides agreed to restart talks; military-to-military communications were restored at a meeting in Abu Dhabi.

question_text: In which year was the New START Treaty originally signed before it expired in February 2026?
explanation: The New START Treaty was signed in Prague on April 8, 2010, by US President Barack Obama and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, entering into force in 2011. It capped each side's deployed strategic nuclear warheads at 1,550 and expired on February 5, 2026.

question_text: A new Israel-Hezbollah war began on March 2, 2026, killing over 2,000 people in which country?
explanation: The new Israel-Hezbollah war began on March 2, 2026, killing more than 2,000 people in Lebanon. A 10-day ceasefire was reached on April 17, 2026, after talks in Washington on April 14-15, 2026.

question_text: When and where were the talks held that produced the April 17, 2026 Israel-Lebanon ceasefire?
explanation: Talks held in Washington from April 14-15, 2026, produced a 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire announced on April 17, 2026, halting the Israel-Hezbollah war that had begun on March 2, 2026 and killed over 2,000 in Lebanon.

question_text: Under what name did the US and Israel launch joint strikes against Iran on February 28, 2026, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei on day one?
explanation: The US and Israel launched 'Operation Epic Fury' against Iran on February 28, 2026. Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed on day one of the strikes. The operation marked a major escalation of the West Asia conflict.

question_text: Which Iranian leader was killed on the first day of 'Operation Epic Fury' (February 28, 2026)?
explanation: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed on the first day of 'Operation Epic Fury' (February 28, 2026), a joint US-Israel air campaign. Khamenei had been Supreme Leader since 1989. The strike triggered global oil price spikes and emergency UN meetings.

question_text: The US-Iran talks held on April 11-12, 2026, mediated by Pakistan, took place in which city and ended in failure?
explanation: Pakistan mediated US-Iran talks at Islamabad on April 11-12, 2026, which ended in failure. The talks were held in the aftermath of 'Operation Epic Fury' (Feb 28, 2026) which had killed Ayatollah Khamenei, and amid ongoing tensions across West Asia.

question_text: Who was elected President of Myanmar on April 9, 2026, securing 429 of 584 electoral college votes?
explanation: Senior General Min Aung Hlaing, the junta chief who led the 2021 coup, was elected President of Myanmar on April 9, 2026, with 429/584 electoral college votes. General Soe Win was appointed army chief. Critics rejected the polls as a façade for continued military rule.

question_text: Who was sworn in as Nepal's 47th and youngest-ever Prime Minister on March 27, 2026, at the age of 35?
explanation: Balen Shah (rapper-turned-politician, former Mayor of Kathmandu) was sworn in as Nepal's 47th Prime Minister on March 27, 2026 — the youngest ever at age 35. His predecessor KP Sharma Oli was arrested on March 28, 2026, for his crackdown on the 2025 Gen-Z protests (76 killed).

question_text: Which five countries began two-year terms as UN Security Council non-permanent members on January 1, 2026 (term 2026-27)?
option_a: Algeria, Guyana, ROK, Sierra Leone, Slovenia
option_b: Bahrain, Colombia, DR Congo, Latvia, Liberia
explanation: The UNGA elected Bahrain (186 votes), DR Congo (183), Liberia (181), Colombia (180) and Latvia (178) on June 3, 2025, as UNSC non-permanent members for the 2026-27 term. Latvia is a first-time member. They replaced Algeria, Guyana, South Korea, Sierra Leone and Slovenia (term 2024-25).

question_text: Who is the President of the European Council since December 1, 2024?
explanation: António Costa (Portugal), former PM of Portugal (2015-2024), is the President of the European Council since December 1, 2024, succeeding Charles Michel (Belgium). Ursula von der Leyen (Germany) continues as President of the European Commission (her 2nd term began December 2024).

question_text: On which date in 2026 did India and the European Union conclude the 'Mother of all Free Trade Deals' at the 16th EU-India Summit in New Delhi?
explanation: India and the EU concluded their long-awaited Free Trade Agreement on January 27, 2026, at the 16th EU-India Summit in New Delhi. EC President Ursula von der Leyen called it 'the mother of all deals', creating a free trade zone of ~2 billion people. A Security & Defence Partnership and a mobility/migration pact were also signed.

question_text: Which country holds the ASEAN Chairmanship for 2026, with the theme 'Navigating Our Future, Together'?
explanation: The Philippines holds the ASEAN Chairmanship for 2026 (theme: 'Navigating Our Future, Together'), under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The 48th ASEAN Summit was held in Cebu on May 8-9, 2026. Priorities: regional energy & food security, South China Sea Code of Conduct, ASEAN nationals' safety. Malaysia was Chair in 2025; Singapore is set to chair 2027.

question_text: The 48th ASEAN Summit was held in May 2026 in which Philippine city?
explanation: The 48th ASEAN Summit was held in Cebu, Philippines, on May 8-9, 2026, under the Philippines' 2026 chairship. The 49th ASEAN Summit is scheduled for November 2026. ASEAN's 11 members now include Timor-Leste, admitted at the 47th ASEAN Summit (Kuala Lumpur, October 2025).

question_text: The 27th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) was held in October 2024 in which country — the first CHOGM in a Pacific Small Island Developing State and the first chaired by King Charles III?
explanation: CHOGM 2024 was held in Apia, Samoa, on October 25-26, 2024 — the first CHOGM in a Pacific SIDS and the first chaired by King Charles III as Head of the Commonwealth. The summit adopted the 'Apia Commonwealth Ocean Declaration for One Resilient Common Future' and elected Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey (Ghana) as next Secretary-General. The Commonwealth has 56 member states.

question_text: Who became the 7th Commonwealth Secretary-General on April 1, 2025 — the first woman from Africa to hold the office?
explanation: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey (Ghana), a former Foreign Minister of Ghana (2017-2024), assumed office as the 7th Commonwealth Secretary-General on April 1, 2025 — the first woman from Africa in the post. She was elected at CHOGM 2024 in Apia, Samoa, succeeding Baroness Patricia Scotland (Dominica/UK). Commonwealth HQ: Marlborough House, London.

question_text: Who assumed office as the 12th Director-General of UNESCO on November 15, 2025, becoming the first Director-General from an Arab country?
explanation: Khaled El-Enany (Egypt), an Egyptologist and former Minister of Tourism & Antiquities, was elected DG of UNESCO in November 2025 with 172/174 votes and assumed office on November 15, 2025. He is the first DG from an Arab country and the second from Africa (after Senegal's Amadou-Mahtar Mbow). He succeeded Audrey Azoulay (France). UNESCO HQ: Paris.

question_text: COP30 was held in Belém, Brazil, in November 2025. What was the name of its main outcome document, a Portuguese term meaning 'collective efforts'?
explanation: The COP30 main outcome document is called the 'global mutirão' — Portuguese for 'collective efforts'. COP30 ran November 10-22, 2025, in Belém, on the edge of the Amazon. Key outcomes: pledge to mobilise $1.3 trillion/year by 2035, triple adaptation finance by 2035, and launch of the Tropical Forest Forever Fund ($6.6 bn raised). The summit fell short of an explicit fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap.

question_text: The 'Tropical Forest Forever Fund' (TFFF), launched at COP30 in Belém (November 2025), rewards countries for what action?
explanation: The Tropical Forest Forever Fund (TFFF) — a Brazil-led mechanism launched at COP30, Belém (Nov 2025) — rewards countries for conserving tropical forests. It raised $6.6 billion with 53 country signatories. The fund supplements REDD+ and aims to provide predictable, performance-based finance for forest protection in the Global South.

question_text: The 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14), held March 26-29, 2026, was hosted in which African capital — only the second WTO Ministerial held in Africa?
explanation: MC14 was held at the Palais des Congrès in Yaoundé, Cameroon, from March 26-29, 2026 — only the second WTO Ministerial Conference hosted in Africa, after MC10 in Nairobi (2015). DG Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (in her 2nd term) chaired discussions on dispute settlement reform, fisheries subsidies, and the e-commerce moratorium.

question_text: Which country holds the G7 Presidency in 2026 and will host the 52nd G7 Summit at Évian-les-Bains on June 15-17, 2026?
explanation: France holds the G7 Presidency for 2026 (its first since the 2019 Biarritz Summit). The 52nd G7 Summit will be held at Évian-les-Bains, Haute-Savoie, on June 15-17, 2026. President Emmanuel Macron set priorities around reducing global inequality and safeguarding financial stability. Canada hosted G7 2025 (Kananaskis).

question_text: The 25th SCO Heads of State Summit — the largest in SCO history — was held in August-September 2025 in which Chinese city?
explanation: The 25th SCO Summit was held in Tianjin, China, on August 31 - September 1, 2025 — the largest SCO summit ever. Key outcomes: Tianjin Declaration; SCO Development Strategy 2026-2035; agreement to establish an SCO Development Bank; Laos accepted as a partner (taking SCO to a 27-nation family). PM Modi attended; Kyrgyzstan took over rotating SCO presidency for 2025-26.

question_text: Which major financial institution did SCO members agree to establish at the Tianjin Summit (September 2025)?
explanation: SCO members agreed at the Tianjin Summit (Sept 2025) to establish an SCO Development Bank to finance infrastructure and economic programmes — a long-discussed Chinese proposal. Other agreements: SCO Universal Center for Countering Security Challenges and Threats, Information Security Center, Center for Combating Transnational Organized Crime, and Anti-Drug Center.

question_text: Which of the following is NOT a BRICS Partner Country (a separate category introduced at the Kazan Summit 2024) as of 2026?
explanation: BRICS Partner Countries (introduced at Kazan 2024) as of 2026 are: Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam (10 partners). Pakistan is NOT a BRICS partner. With 10 full members + 10 partners, BRICS-20 covers ~55-56% of world population.

question_text: The 19th BRICS Summit, under India's 2026 chairmanship (theme 'Vikasam for All'), is scheduled for which month in India?
explanation: India is hosting the 19th BRICS Summit in August-September 2026 under its 2026 chairmanship. The BRICS-2026 logo and theme 'Vikasam for All' (Development for All) were launched on January 13, 2026. India assumed the BRICS chair on January 1, 2026, succeeding Brazil.

question_text: ICC Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan stepped aside in May 2025 amid a UN-led inquiry into misconduct allegations. Which two officials took over the Office's day-to-day functions?
option_b: Nazhat Shameem Khan and Mame Mandiaye Niang
option_c: Luis Moreno Ocampo and Cherif Bassiouni
explanation: After Karim Khan (UK) stepped aside in May 2025 pending a UN OIOS inquiry into misconduct allegations (which he denies), Deputy Prosecutors Nazhat Shameem Khan (Fiji) and Mame Mandiaye Niang (Senegal) took the lead at the ICC Office of the Prosecutor. The ICC is headquartered in The Hague; in November 2024 it issued arrest warrants against Israeli PM Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Gallant.

question_text: Which US administration activated sanctions against International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors and judges in February 2025?
explanation: President Donald Trump (second term, from January 20, 2025) signed an executive order on February 6, 2025, imposing sanctions on ICC prosecutors and judges over the November 2024 arrest warrants against Israeli PM Netanyahu and former DM Gallant. The US is not an ICC member; the Rome Statute (1998) governs the Court.

question_text: Who is the Secretary-General of the OECD since June 1, 2021, and was re-appointed for a second 5-year term?
explanation: Mathias Cormann (Australia), former Australian Finance Minister, is the 6th OECD Secretary-General since June 1, 2021, and was re-appointed for a second 5-year term (2026-2031). The OECD (HQ: Paris) has 38 members; current accession candidates include Argentina, Indonesia, Brazil, Peru, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia and Thailand. India is a 'Key Partner' (applied 2023).

question_text: UNESCO Director-General Khaled El-Enany (in office from November 15, 2025) is from which country?
explanation: Khaled El-Enany is from Egypt — a renowned Egyptologist and former Egyptian Minister of Tourism & Antiquities (2019-2022). He is UNESCO's 12th DG, the first from an Arab country, elected in November 2025 with 172 of 174 votes. Campaign slogan: 'UNESCO for the People'.

question_text: Following the admission of Timor-Leste at the 47th ASEAN Summit (Kuala Lumpur, October 2025), how many full members does ASEAN have as of 2026?
explanation: ASEAN has 11 full members as of 2026, after Timor-Leste (East Timor) was admitted as the 11th member at the 47th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur (October 2025) — the first ASEAN expansion since Cambodia joined in 1999. The 10 prior members: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam. ASEAN Secretariat: Jakarta.

question_text: India has formally bid to serve as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for which two-year term — which would be its 9th term if elected?
explanation: India has formally bid for a UNSC non-permanent seat for 2028-29 (representing Asia-Pacific regional group)—its 9th term if elected. India's eight prior UNSC terms: 1950-51 (founding period), 1967-68, 1972-73, 1977-78, 1984-85, 1991-92, 2011-12, 2021-22 (most recent). The 2028-29 bid reflects India's institutional commitment to global governance. Simultaneously, India, as part of the G4 coalition (Brazil, Germany, Japan), continues advocating for UNSC permanent membership expansion to reflect 21st-century geopolitics: (1) India's 1.4B+ population, major developing economy, permanent security council membership justification, (2) Germany as Europe's largest economy (excluded since WWII), (3) Brazil as Latin America's leading power, (4) Japan as Asia's technological leader. G4 unified position: UNSC expansion from 5 permanent members to 11 (adding India, Brazil, Germany, Japan + 2 African representatives) would improve legitimacy and representativeness. Obstacles: P5 (especially China, Russia) oppose expansion diluting their veto power; developing countries contest P5 expansion inequity. India's dual strategy: secure repeat non-permanent seats while long-term pushing permanent membership—demonstrating sustained commitment to multilateral governance and Global South leadership.

question_text: The G20 Leaders' Summit 2025 was held in which city, marking the first-ever G20 hosted on the African continent?
explanation: The 20th G20 Summit was held at the Johannesburg Expo Centre, South Africa on November 22-23, 2025 — first G20 ever hosted on the African continent, signalling a historic shift in global economic governance toward the Global South. South Africa's G20 presidency (under President Cyril Ramaphosa) prioritized African development, debt sustainability, and UN Security Council reform — pushing back against Western dominance in multilateral institutions. India played a bridging role in supporting consensus on climate finance and development priorities. South Africa's presidency followed Brazil (2024) and handed over to the USA (2026), marking a reversal in Global South leadership. The Johannesburg Declaration adopted a 122-point agenda emphasizing Ubuntu philosophy (African values of interconnectedness), signalling Africa's centrality to 21st-century development discourse.

question_text: What was the official theme of South Africa's G20 Presidency and Johannesburg Summit 2025?
explanation: 'Solidarity, Equality, Sustainability' was South Africa's G20 2025 theme, rooted in the African Ubuntu philosophy meaning 'I am because we are.' The 122-point Johannesburg Declaration operationalized this tri-pillar vision: Solidarity=multilateral cooperation free from hegemony, Equality=fair economic opportunities for the Global South with debt relief, Sustainability=long-term development without sacrificing climate commitments. The theme directly challenged Western consensus-building and elevated African/Global South priorities in climate finance, technology transfer, and UN reform. India endorsed this pro-South positioning, aligning with its own G20 2023 focus on inclusive development. The declaration's unprecedented adoption at the summit's OPENING (not closing) signalled South Africa's determination to proceed with multilateral outcomes regardless of US absence.

question_text: Which major G20 member was ABSENT from the G20 Johannesburg Summit 2025?
explanation: The USA did not participate in the G20 Johannesburg Summit 2025 — a symbolic statement reflecting Trump's transactional foreign policy and diminished multilateral engagement. President Trump's absence, coupled with Secretary Blinken's limited representation, signalled a withdrawal from Global South consensus-building. This prompted South Africa to adopt the 122-point declaration at the summit's opening regardless of US participation, demonstrating that multilateral outcomes are achievable without hegemonic consensus. Argentina was the only nation PRESENT that did not subscribe to the final declaration — FM Quirno cited missing 'geopolitical context' on the ongoing Iran-Israel-US war (2026), highlighting Global North-South divides on Middle East diplomacy. India capitalized on this moment to reinforce South-South cooperation and assert Indian diplomatic leadership within BRICS and the developing world coalition.

question_text: The Johannesburg G20 2025 Declaration referenced 'Ubuntu' philosophy. Ubuntu is a concept from which tradition?
option_c: African philosophy emphasising interconnectedness and shared humanity
explanation: Ubuntu is a Bantu philosophical concept meaning 'I am because we are' — emphasising interconnectedness, collective responsibility, and shared humanity over individualism. South Africa embedded this into the G20 Johannesburg 2025 Declaration as a deliberate counter-narrative to Western liberal individualism and neoliberal economics. Ubuntu became the foundational principle for the theme 'Solidarity, Equality, Sustainability,' positioning African wisdom traditions as legitimate frameworks for global governance. The choice signalled South Africa's assertion of African intellectual authority and rejected Western hegemony in defining development models. India resonated with Ubuntu's parallels to concepts like 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family), enabling India-South Africa coordination on Global South interests.

question_text: The G20 Johannesburg 2025 Declaration included a call for reform of which major international body?
explanation: The 122-point G20 Johannesburg Declaration called for UN Security Council (UNSC) reform — a long-standing demand by Global South nations (India, Brazil, South Africa) who seek permanent seats reflecting 21st-century geopolitical realities. The UNSC call reflected frustration with Cold War-era structures perpetuating Western dominance. India strongly backed UNSC reform alongside African representation, positioning itself as a voice for systemic global governance restructuring. Other landmark outcomes included: G20 Critical Minerals Framework (voluntary supply-chain tracking), 'Mission 300' (electrify 300 million Africans by 2030), AI for Africa initiative, universal early warning systems for climate/disaster by 2027, debt sustainability mechanisms for developing nations, and a Debt Sustainability Framework addressing the debt crisis facing small island states and LDCs.

question_text: Which country will host the G20 Summit in 2026?
explanation: USA will host the G20 in Miami in 2026 — a transition marking return of Western dominance in G20 leadership after Global South chairs (Brazil 2024, South Africa 2025). The chairmanship was formally handed over from South Africa to the USA on January 12, 2026 (a low-key, offsite ceremony reflecting US absence from Johannesburg). India's G20 presidency (2023) had advanced the African Union's permanent membership and Development Agenda priorities; USA's 2026 presidency is expected to emphasize economic competition, digital economy regulation, and Indo-Pacific security architecture — competing with China's influence in BRICS and regional forums. Host sequence: Brazil (2024) → South Africa (2025) → USA/Miami (2026).

question_text: At the G20 Johannesburg 2025, what voluntary framework was endorsed for managing critical mineral supply chains?
explanation: The G20 Critical Minerals Framework (voluntary, non-binding) was endorsed at Johannesburg 2025 — establishing governance principles for tracking supply chains, labour costs, environmental damages, and community impacts in mining. Framework recognizes minerals (lithium, cobalt, rare earths) critical for green energy transition are concentrated in few countries, creating geopolitical vulnerabilities. India, as both a consumer (EV manufacturing ramp-up) and producer (rare earths), supported principles emphasizing developing-nation access to technology and fair pricing. The framework is deliberately voluntary to secure buy-in from major mining nations (Australia, Indonesia, Peru) and avoid binding commitments affecting sovereignty. This followed parallel work at G7 Kananaskis 2025, showing coordination between competing forums on supply-chain risk.

question_text: Which nation opposed the G20 Johannesburg 2025 final declaration, citing missing geopolitical context on the Middle East?
explanation: Argentina was the only G20 nation PRESENT that did not subscribe to the Johannesburg 2025 Declaration — a symbolic dissent reflecting Argentina's pro-US alignment under President Javier Milei (elected 2023). Argentine FM Julio Quirno stated 'context and geopolitical facts' were critically missing regarding the Middle East (the escalating Iran-Israel-US war, February 28-April 8, 2026). Argentina's refusal to sign signalled divergence from Global South consensus and alignment with Western positions on Middle East intervention. The USA was entirely absent from the summit, making Argentina's dissent the sole internal opposition. India and other G20 members supported the declaration despite geopolitical complexity, endorsing South Africa's framing of Ubuntu-inspired multilateralism as superior to bifurcated Cold War logics.

question_text: The G7 Summit 2025 was hosted by which country, and who was the host leader?
explanation: Canada hosted the 51st G7 Summit at Kananaskis, Alberta in the Rocky Mountains (June 15-17, 2025). PM Mark Carney (newly elected Feb 2025) hosted in a remote location partly for security. Trump's early departure (~12 hours) citing the escalating Israel-Iran Twelve-Day War (June 2025) disrupted cohesion, reflecting Trump's transactional foreign policy and skepticism of multilateral commitment. The remaining six G7 members (EU, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada) issued a separate statement on AI and critical minerals without the US, signalling that G7 cohesion was fragmenting. No formal joint communiqué was signed after Trump's exit, weakening G7 political authority. This recalled Trump's 2018 Charlevoix early departure and foreshadowed broader unilateral US posturing in 2026.

question_text: At which specific location in Canada was the G7 Summit 2025 held?
explanation: G7 Summit 2025 was held in Kananaskis, Alberta — a remote mountain resort in the Canadian Rockies chosen for security and symbolic separation from public/media scrutiny. The isolation also insulated against anti-globalization protests. After Trump's abrupt early departure, the remaining six G7 leaders (France, Germany, Italy, Japan, UK, Canada, EU) issued a joint statement without the US on AI governance, quantum computing, critical minerals, wildfire cooperation, and migrant smuggling networks — signalling that G7 could function without US consensus. This demonstrated the fragility of Western multilateral institutions under Trump's transactional approach and elevated alternatives (EU-Japan-India coordination on Indo-Pacific security) as substitute frameworks.

question_text: US President Trump departed the G7 Kananaskis Summit 2025 early, citing which international crisis?
explanation: Trump left G7 Kananaskis early (after ~12 hours on June 15, 2025) citing the Israel-Iran conflict — specifically the escalating June 2025 Twelve-Day War (June 2-13) involving sustained Israeli strikes on Iranian military infrastructure and Iranian retaliation. Trump's framing centered on US interests in Middle East military dominance rather than G7 consensus-building, consistent with his 'America First' doctrine. His departure recalled his 2018 Charlevoix G7 early exit and signalled that Trump prioritizes bilateral US interests over multilateral institutions. The remaining six G7 leaders (Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, EU) issued a joint statement without the US, demonstrating resilience of G7 minus-one diplomacy and concern that the Western alliance was fragmenting under American unilateralism.

question_text: What tariff threat did Trump make toward Canada after the G7 Kananaskis Summit 2025?
option_c: 35% tariff on Canadian goods if no trade deal reached
explanation: Trump threatened 35% tariffs on Canadian goods (effective August 1, 2025) if Canada did not reach a swift trade deal renegotiating USMCA. Trump's aggressive tariff coercion against G7 allies (especially Canada and UK) was a defining tension of Kananaskis, undermining Western trade cohesion. His threats signalled a protectionist turn contradicting traditional G7 trade liberalism and creating economic fragmentation. India viewed this as validation of its own strategic autonomy and reduced reliance on Western markets, accelerating India-ASEAN, India-EU FTA, and BRICS de-dollarization initiatives. G7 2026 will be hosted by France in Évian-les-Bains (June 15-17), where trade tensions are expected to dominate discussions.

question_text: The G7 Kananaskis 2025 remaining six leaders' joint statement reached consensus on which topics?
option_c: AI, quantum computing, and critical minerals
explanation: The six remaining G7 leaders (without Trump/USA) reached consensus on AI, quantum computing, and critical minerals supply-chain security. The statement emphasized AI should 'grow prosperity, benefit societies, and address global challenges' — signalling a pro-innovation stance balancing regulation with economic growth. This marked a shift from prior G7 AI governance focus (COP29, COP30) which prioritized existential risks. The joint statement demonstrated that G7 minus the US could still project technical authority and coordinate on technology standards. India noted this as validation of plurilateral formats (QUAD, I2U2, ALBA) as alternatives to G7/G20 consensus when Western unity fractured. Critical minerals language aligned with India's interests in ensuring developing-nation access to clean-tech supply chains.

question_text: Which country will host the G7 Summit in 2026?
explanation: France will host the G7 Summit in 2026 at Évian-les-Bains (June 15-17, 2026) — second time France hosted at Évian (previous summit 2003). President Emmanuel Macron, re-elected 2022, will lead as France asserts European autonomy from Trump's unilateralism. Évian 2026 is expected to address transatlantic tensions, European defense spending, NATO cohesion, and China-Russia containment. Host sequence: Italy Puglia (2024) → Canada Kananaskis (2025) → France Évian (2026). G7 members: USA, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan + EU. India views France's hosting as an opportunity for stronger India-EU FTA implementation (signed Jan 27, 2026) and coordination on Indo-Pacific security independent of US leadership.

question_text: The NATO Summit 2025 was held in which city on June 24-25, 2025?
explanation: NATO Summit 2025 was held at the World Forum, The Hague, Netherlands on June 24-25, 2025 — months after Trump's return to power raised questions about NATO's Article 5 commitment. Secretary-General Mark Rutte (Netherlands, ex-PM) presided over the largest NATO expenditure increase since Cold War. Key outcomes: 5% GDP defense spending target (all members except Spain), €40 billion Ukraine aid package, Article 5 commitment reaffirmed despite Trump's earlier skepticism, NATO Strategy updated. India observed NATO expansion as geopolitically significant for Indo-Pacific security (Australia, Japan, South Korea coordination through NATO). NATO 2026 will be in Ankara, Turkey (July 7-8), further involving NATO in broader Indo-Pacific deterrence against China-Russia alignment. NATO now has 32 members (Sweden joined March 2024).

question_text: The most significant outcome of NATO Hague Summit 2025 was a new defense spending target. What was it?
explanation: NATO Hague 2025 adopted 5% GDP defense spending — a seismic jump from the 2014 Wales Summit benchmark of 2%, reflecting escalating Russian threats post-2022 Ukraine invasion and new China-Russia-Iran axis dynamics. Breakdown: 3.5% core military capabilities + 1.5% defense-related (cyber, infrastructure, space, nuclear). All 32 NATO members agreed except Spain (PM Sánchez resisted). This represents NATO's largest peacetime rearmament, with combined annual defense budgets approaching $2 trillion. India noted this militarization of Europe creates vulnerabilities for India's defense exports and arms-control advocacy; simultaneously, it validates India's own defense modernization against Pakistan-China nexus. The 5% target signalled Western resolve to deter Russian expansion and contain Chinese military growth in hybrid domains.

question_text: Under NATO's 5% GDP defense spending target (The Hague 2025), how is the spending broken down?
option_d: All 5% directed to direct military capabilities
explanation: NATO's 5% GDP target (Hague 2025): 3.5% for core military capabilities (hardware, personnel, readiness) + 1.5% for broader defense-related sectors (cyber defense, space operations, infrastructure, intelligence, nuclear deterrence). This split reflects modern hybrid warfare where kinetic and non-kinetic domains are equally critical. The structure allows NATO members flexibility in allocating budgets while maintaining credible conventional + cyber + nuclear deterrence. India, as a non-NATO developing democracy, views the NATO budget increase as validation of defense spending increases needed for its Pakistan/China deterrence while simultaneously pressuring Indian defense budgets upward. The framework replaces the 2014 Wales Summit target of 2% GDP, representing a 150% increase in spending intensity.

question_text: Which NATO member was the sole dissenter to the 5% defense spending target at the Hague Summit 2025?
explanation: Spain was the only NATO member that did not agree to the 5% GDP defense spending target at The Hague Summit 2025. PM Pedro Sánchez's Socialist government historically resisted NATO defense escalation, citing domestic social spending priorities and pacifist constituencies. Spain's dissent reflected broader European tensions between welfare expansion and defense militarization. This isolated Spain diplomatically and raised questions about NATO consensus-building when facing Russian threats. All 31 other members (including Poland, Romania, Slovakia near Russian borders) supported the 5% target. NATO now has 32 members after Sweden joined as the 32nd member on March 7, 2024 (Finland joined 2023, upgrading NATO's Russia border coverage). Spain's position was overridden by alliance supermajority, foreshadowing challenges for binding NATO decisions when member interests diverge.

question_text: How much financial aid did NATO allies pledge to Ukraine at the Hague Summit 2025?
explanation: NATO allies pledged €40 billion in defense aid to Ukraine for 2025 at the Hague Summit (June 24-25, 2025). The commitment represented escalating Western military support as Russia-Ukraine war intensified into its 4th year. Notably, the declaration did NOT include a Ukraine NATO membership invitation, formal timeline, or clear pathway — disappointing President Zelenskyy's hopes for stronger political commitments. NATO leadership wanted to avoid direct confrontation with Russia while maintaining Ukraine's morale. Instead, NATO emphasized enhanced military capacity-building and intelligence sharing. India maintained strict neutrality on Ukraine aid questions, criticizing both sides' geopolitical adventurism while opposing unilateral economic sanctions. The €40 billion demonstrated NATO's military commitment while avoiding irreversible escalation (no-fly zone, NATO troops on ground).

question_text: Where will the NATO Summit 2026 be held?
explanation: NATO Summit 2026 will be held July 7-8, 2026 at the Beştepe Presidential Complex in Ankara, Turkey — a symbolically significant location highlighting Turkey's geopolitical centrality to NATO (controlling Bosphorus Strait, managing Syria border, balancing Russia-West relations). President Erdoğan's hosting will emphasize Turkish mediation role and NATO's southeastern flank against Russian/Iranian influence. NATO Secretary-General since October 2024: Mark Rutte (Netherlands, ex-PM), who replaced Jens Stoltenberg (10 years). India views Turkey's role as pivotal for Indo-Pacific NATO expansion (Australia, Japan, South Korea partnerships) and Istanbul as a strategic hub for Asia-Europe connectivity. Turkey's NATO membership also complicates NATO-India-QUAD coordination on China containment. Host sequence: Washington DC (2024) → The Hague (2025) → Ankara (2026).

question_text: The 17th BRICS Summit 2025 was hosted by which country, and where?
explanation: The 17th BRICS Summit 2025 was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on July 6-7, 2025 — Brazil's BRICS Chairmanship year and the first BRICS summit to feature Indonesia (11th full member, joined Jan 6, 2025) and 10 partner countries admitted at Rio. Brazil's President Lula positioned BRICS as a counterweight to Western-dominated IMF/World Bank through new BRICS Development Bank initiatives and de-dollarization proposals. This was a watershed moment: BRICS now represents 37% of global GDP (PPP) and 45% of world population, with expansion into Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Malaysia partner), Africa, and Central Asia signalling a deliberate Global South realignment. India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi (Sept 12-13, 2026) as BRICS Chair 2026, deepening India's leadership in non-aligned Global South diplomacy and asserting India as BRICS's Asia-Pacific anchor.

question_text: Which country joined BRICS as a full member on January 6, 2025, becoming the first Southeast Asian nation in the bloc?
explanation: Indonesia joined BRICS as a full member on January 6, 2025 — first Southeast Asian state in BRICS and the 11th full member, breaking BRICS's previous concentration in Africa, Russia, and Asia. Indonesia's bid was approved at BRICS Kazan 2024 summit but deferred entry until after Indonesia's October 2024 presidential election (Prabowo Subianto elected). Indonesia's accession was geopolitically momentous: a 270+ million population Southeast Asian democracy joining a bloc historically dominated by authoritarian regimes, signalling BRICS's broadening legitimacy and reach. India strongly supported Indonesia's entry as it balances China's influence within BRICS. Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand remain partner countries (not full members). BRICS full members now: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia.

question_text: At BRICS Rio Summit 2025, how many new countries were admitted as BRICS 'partner countries'?
explanation: 10 new BRICS partner countries admitted at Rio 2025: Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, and Vietnam. These create a two-tier BRICS structure: 11 full members + 10 partner nations = 21 total members representing alternative blocs (SCO members like Kazakhstan/Uzbekistan, Latin American solidarity with Cuba/Bolivia, African growth markets). Partner status provides access to BRICS development finance, trade cooperation, and digital currency initiatives without full voting rights. India supported expansion as it dilutes China's influence by bringing in Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan (India partners on Central Asia), and Malaysia/Vietnam (India's Act East allies). The 21-member formation positions BRICS as genuinely Global South representing non-aligned nations and creating institutional alternatives to US-led multilateralism.

question_text: After Indonesia joined in 2025, how many FULL MEMBERS does BRICS have?
explanation: BRICS has 11 full members: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa (original 5, founded 2011) + Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia (joined January 1, 2024, BRICS+ expansion announced Kazan 2024) + Indonesia (January 6, 2025). The 10 partner countries at Rio 2025 (Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, Vietnam) are NOT full members and lack voting rights in BRICS decisions. Total BRICS structure: 11 full members + 10 partners = 21 nations. India plays a crucial balancing role within BRICS, mediating between China-Russia strategic alignment and the broader development/non-aligned agenda. India's 2026 BRICS Chairmanship will likely emphasize inclusive development and technology transfer over geopolitical confrontation.

question_text: Where will the 18th BRICS Summit 2026 be held?
explanation: 18th BRICS Summit 2026 is in New Delhi, India on September 12-13, 2026 — India's BRICS Chairmanship year. This is India's first BRICS leaders' summit since the 2024-2025 expansion to 11 full members and 10 partners, positioning India to shape BRICS's post-expansion agenda. India's presidency will likely emphasize: South-South cooperation, technology transfer to developing nations, climate justice and loss-and-damage financing (aligned with India's COP presidency advocacy), counterterrorism cooperation (aligned with SCO Tianjin condemnation of Pahalgam attack), and development finance through BRICS Development Bank. New Delhi summit will also showcase India's diplomatic leadership within non-aligned movements and validate India's global stature. Host sequence: Russia Kazan (2024) → Brazil Rio (2025) → India New Delhi (2026) → Egypt (2027).

question_text: Which of these is NOT one of the 10 BRICS partner countries admitted at Rio de Janeiro 2025?
explanation: Pakistan is NOT a BRICS partner country despite SCO membership and Strategic Partnership with China. The 10 BRICS partners (Rio 2025): Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, Vietnam. Pakistan's exclusion from BRICS reflects India-Pakistan antagonism (India's veto power in consensus-based organizations) and Pakistan's closer alignment with China-centric blocs (SCO, China-Pakistan Economic Corridor). India's diplomatic leverage ensures Pakistan cannot enter BRICS without explicit Indian support. Pakistan's focus remains SCO, Shanghai (financial markets), and bilateral relations with China-Saudi Arabia. Notably, Malaysia and Vietnam (India's Act East partners) were admitted as BRICS partners, strengthening India's Southeast Asia engagement through multilateral forums.

question_text: BRICS was originally 'BRIC'. When did South Africa join, and when was the FIRST expansion after that?
option_b: South Africa joined 2010; next expansion January 2024
explanation: South Africa joined BRIC in 2010 (making it BRICS). BRICS remained the original 5 members (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) for 14 years until the first major expansion at BRICS Kazan 2024. First expansion: January 1, 2024 when Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, and Saudi Arabia joined (5 new members, broadening BRICS into Africa, Middle East, Gulf). Indonesia followed January 6, 2025 as the 11th member. Goldman Sachs economist Jim O'Neill coined 'BRIC' in 2001 as an investment thesis; BRICS formalized as political bloc through Shanghai Cooperation 2009. This 14-year stability then rapid 2024-2025 expansion signals BRICS's acceleration as counter-Western institutional alternative and India's crucial role in managing expansion's inclusivity/consensual expansion.

question_text: BRICS full members (11 nations) collectively represent approximately what percentage of global GDP (PPP)?
explanation: BRICS 11 full members represent approximately 37% of global GDP (PPP) as of 2025 — exceeding G7 (30% PPP) and signalling a fundamental rebalancing of economic power from West to Global South. BRICS represents 45%+ of world population (~3.5 billion people). India contributes ~$13 trillion (PPP) to BRICS GDP, positioned second only to China within the bloc. De-dollarization is a key BRICS economic priority (Brazil Lula advanced this at Rio 2025), developing alternatives to USD for trade settlement, currency reserves, and development finance. BRICS Development Bank, BRICS reserve currency proposals, and Common Development Bank are mechanisms to reduce dependence on US-controlled financial architecture (IMF, World Bank, SWIFT). India supports BRICS financial independence while maintaining strategic partnerships with developed economies.

question_text: The 25th SCO Heads of State Summit 2025 was held in which city?
explanation: 25th SCO Heads of State Council was held in Tianjin, China (Bohai Bay, Jinghai District) on August 31-September 1, 2025 — described as the largest SCO summit in history with unprecedented scale. Key outcomes: Tianjin Declaration affirming regional security and multilateralism, SCO Development Bank established (with initial capitalization from China), SCO 2035 Strategy extending SCO's vision beyond 2025, counter-terrorism cooperation programme aligned with India's security priorities, cultural/civilizational dialogue framework. 20 key documents signed. India participated at full leadership level, with PM Modi meeting President Xi Jinping bilaterally (first meeting on Chinese soil in 7 years), signalling India-China normalization post-Galwan tensions. SCO now encompasses 10 full members covering ~30% of world population across Eurasia.

question_text: A significant bilateral at SCO Tianjin 2025: PM Modi met President Xi Jinping. What made this historically notable?
option_b: First time Modi met Xi on Chinese soil in 7 years
option_c: First meeting after India joined SCO in 2017
explanation: PM Modi met Xi Jinping at SCO Tianjin 2025 (September 1, 2025) — first time Modi met Xi on Chinese soil in 7 years (since Wuhan 2018 informal summit). The bilateral signalled India-China normalization post-2020 Galwan clash, with both leaders pledging cooperation on resolving Himalayan border disputes through LAC patrolling agreements (Depsang, Demchok resolved Oct-Nov 2024). Modi outlined India's SCO vision on three pillars: Security (counterterrorism), Connectivity (infrastructure), Opportunity (economic growth). The meeting demonstrated multilateral forums (SCO) can facilitate bilateral reconciliation when direct diplomacy is strained. India's strategic objective: balance China's economic dominance within BRICS/SCO through partnerships with Central Asian nations (Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan) and mediation between Russia-China axis and India-Japan-Australia cooperation.

question_text: What major institutional decision was taken at the SCO Tianjin Summit 2025?
option_b: Establishment of the SCO Development Bank
explanation: SCO Development Bank was established at Tianjin 2025 as a multilateral development financing institution to fund infrastructure, connectivity, and development projects among SCO members — modeled on Asian Development Bank but oriented toward Eurasian corridors. China pledged initial capitalization: 2 billion yuan ($280M) as grant aid + 10 billion yuan ($1.4B) in concessional loans over three years. Bank headquarters: Beijing. This represents SCO's institutional maturation beyond security cooperation into economic integration. India negotiated participation in bank governance to ensure equitable decision-making and prevent Chinese dominance. 20 key documents signed: Tianjin Declaration, SCO 2035 Strategy (vision to 2035), counter-extremism cooperation framework, cultural/civilizational dialogue platform. The bank enables BRICS/SCO members to reduce dependence on Western IMF/World Bank architecture and finance development on South-South basis.

question_text: SCO Tianjin 2025 explicitly condemned which Indian security event — a rare SCO condemnation of terrorism targeting India?
explanation: The SCO Tianjin 2025 declaration explicitly condemned the Pahalgam terror attack (April 22, 2025, Anantnag district, Jammu & Kashmir — 26 civilians killed, mostly tourists, by Pakistan-backed terror groups) and called for bringing perpetrators to justice with SCO member cooperation. This was a significant diplomatic victory for India: China and Pakistan (both SCO full members) joined consensus condemning terrorism in Indian territory — a rare achievement given Pakistan-India antagonism within SCO. The condemnation validated India's counterterrorism priorities and positioned India as a victim of cross-border terrorism deserving multilateral support. India leveraged this to advance SCO Regional Anti-Terrorism Structure (RATS) and counterextremism initiatives. Pakistan's agreement signalled constraints on its terror proxy strategy within multilateral forums. SCO's condemnation was more explicit than typical diplomatic language, reflecting post-Galwan India-China warming and consensus-building within the organization.

question_text: SCO Tianjin 2025 had 10 full members. Which of these is NOT a full SCO member?
explanation: Afghanistan is NOT a full SCO member (holds observer status along with Mongolia, Cambodia, Nepal). 10 full SCO members: China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Iran (joined 2023 as 9th member), Belarus (joined 2024 as 10th member). SCO founded June 15, 2001 in Shanghai from Shanghai Five (1996); HQ: Beijing. Afghanistan's observer status reflects its geopolitical sensitivity — Taliban governance creates complications for consensus, though all SCO members have tacitly accepted Taliban rule post-2021. India prioritizes SCO cooperation on Afghanistan counterterrorism and Central Asia stability despite Afghan complications. Belarus's 2024 accession strengthened Russia's hand within SCO, offsetting India-Japan-USA partnerships and complicating consensus on Non-Aligned Movement issues.

question_text: PM Modi outlined India's SCO vision at Tianjin 2025 under three pillars. Which is NOT one of those three?
explanation: PM Modi's three-pillar SCO vision at Tianjin 2025: (1) Security = regional counterterrorism, cybersecurity, maritime safety in shared waters; (2) Connectivity = infrastructure corridors (Central Asia to India, Belt-and-Road alternatives), digital infrastructure, supply-chain resilience; (3) Opportunity = shared economic growth, technology transfer, development cooperation, cultural exchange. 'Democracy' was NOT a pillar, reflecting India's pragmatic approach within SCO's mixed-regime membership (autocracies and democracies). Modi also proposed establishing a Civilizational Dialogue Forum within SCO to address shared cultural heritage, philosophical traditions (Buddhism, Hinduism, Islam), and people-to-people connectivity beyond state-to-state relations. This framework positions India as a bridge between Eurasian civilizations while advancing development priorities aligned with BRICS Global South agenda.

question_text: The 47th ASEAN Summit 2025 was held in which city, and which country chaired ASEAN in 2025?
explanation: 47th ASEAN Summit was held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia on October 26-28, 2025 with Malaysia as ASEAN Chair. Malaysia's presidency prioritized ASEAN centrality in Indo-Pacific architecture, Myanmar crisis resolution, and economic integration amid China-USA strategic competition. Key outcomes: Timor-Leste admitted as 11th member (first expansion since Cambodia 1999), Thailand-Cambodia KL Peace Accord (Trump and PM Anwar witnessed), ASEAN-China FTA 3.0 Upgrade, South China Sea code-of-conduct progress, energy security, food security initiatives. India participated as a key dialogue partner, advancing Act East Policy and India-ASEAN maritime cooperation (QUAD-at-Sea operationalized June 2025). Chairmanship formally passed to Philippines (ASEAN alphabetical rotation). ASEAN now represents 11 member economies with ~700 million population across Indo-Pacific critical for India's strategic autonomy.

question_text: Which country became the 11th member of ASEAN at the Kuala Lumpur Summit October 2025?
explanation: Timor-Leste (East Timor) was formally admitted as ASEAN's 11th member at the 47th ASEAN Summit on October 26, 2025 — ASEAN's first expansion since Cambodia joined in 1999 (26-year gap). Timor-Leste gained independence from Indonesia on May 20, 2002 (strategic date symbolizing India's independence and ASEAN enlargement coordination), sought ASEAN membership since 2011 through multiple applications. Admission strengthens ASEAN's Pacific reach and maritime authority; Timor-Leste controls strategic chokepoints in Timor Sea oil/gas fields (disputed with Australia). India supports Timor-Leste as part of Act East Policy expansion and regional stability. ASEAN HQ: Jakarta, Indonesia. ASEAN now spans from Thailand/Cambodia westward through Indonesia/Philippines to Timor-Leste eastward, encompassing major Indo-Pacific sea lanes critical for India's maritime security.

question_text: The 'Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord' signed at ASEAN 47th Summit 2025 was between which two nations?
explanation: Thailand and Cambodia signed the 'Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord' at the 47th ASEAN Summit 2025 (October 26, 2025) with President Trump and PM Anwar Ibrahim (Malaysia) as witnesses. Accord commits both nations to: permanent ceasefire along disputed border, withdrawal of heavy weapons from border, deployment of third-party observers for monitoring, and Bangkok releasing 18 Cambodian detainees. Thailand-Cambodia border tensions (pre-colonial kingdom disputes, 2008-2011 armed skirmishes) threatened regional stability; Trump's mediation signalled US renewed interest in Southeast Asian dispute resolution. India viewed accord as positive for ASEAN stability and demonstrated multilateral alternatives to bilateral antagonism. Trump simultaneously signed trade deals with Malaysia and Cambodia, establishing US economic presence as counter to Chinese economic dominance in Southeast Asia. ASEAN centrality in mediating intra-regional conflicts remains critical for Indo-Pacific order stability.

question_text: ASEAN KL 2025 upgraded trade architecture with China through which agreement?
option_d: ASEAN Plus Three Trade Modernisation Pact
explanation: ASEAN-China FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol was signed at ASEAN KL 2025 — deepening regional economic integration with China (ASEAN's largest external trade partner, ~20% of ASEAN trade in goods). The protocol modernized rules of origin, services liberalization, investment protections, and digital trade provisions from earlier versions. FTA evolution: Version 1.0 signed 2002 (early economic opening), Version 2.0 in 2015 (post-AEC launch), Version 3.0 in 2025 (digital, green trade, supply-chain resilience). India negotiated with ASEAN for India-ASEAN FTA upgrades to compete with China's economic dominance. ASEAN plays a hedging strategy between US-China competition, seeking maximum economic benefit from both while maintaining independence. China remains ASEAN's largest trading partner, supplier of manufactured goods, and investor in ASEAN infrastructure (Belt-and-Road Initiative).

question_text: After 47th ASEAN Summit 2025, Malaysia handed the ASEAN Chairmanship to which country for 2026?
explanation: Malaysia formally handed ASEAN Chairmanship to Philippines at the close of the 47th ASEAN Summit (October 28, 2025 closing ceremony). ASEAN Chair sequence follows alphabetical order by English country name: Laos (2024) → Malaysia (2025) → Philippines (2026) → Singapore (2027) → Thailand (2028) → Vietnam (2029). Philippines under President Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr. will chair 48th ASEAN Summit held in Cebu (May 6-8, 2026) under theme 'Navigating Our Future, Together.' ASEAN founded 1967 (Bangkok Declaration, ASEAN-5: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand); expanded to 10 members with Vietnam 1995, Laos/Myanmar 1997, Cambodia 1999; now 11 members after Timor-Leste joined 2025. India engages ASEAN through dialogue partnership and Act East Policy, seeking deeper strategic partnerships independent of US-China bipolarity.

question_text: The ASEAN 47th Summit 2025 reviewed implementation of 'Five-Point Consensus' related to which member country's crisis?
explanation: ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus (adopted April 2021, led by Singapore's PM Lee) addresses Myanmar's crisis following the February 1, 2021 military coup by Myanmar's Armed Forces (Tatmadaw). The five points: (1) dialogue through ASEAN mechanisms, (2) cessation of violence, (3) humanitarian assistance, (4) fact-finding mission, (5) special envoy to facilitate dialogue. At KL 2025, ASEAN leaders reaffirmed that cessation of violence MUST precede elections in Myanmar; agreed to maintain ASEAN Special Envoy (rotating annual appointment) for longer-term engagement. Myanmar remains ASEAN's most pressing challenge: military junta refuses to engage meaningfully, civil disobedience movement and armed resistance continue, humanitarian crisis deepens. India supports ASEAN's consensus approach while maintaining pragmatic engagement with Myanmar junta on security cooperation. Consensus-based ASEAN decision-making allows Myanmar participation despite coup, preventing Myanmar's exit while maintaining diplomatic pressure.

question_text: COP30 was held in which city in November 2025, symbolically located in the Amazon rainforest?
explanation: COP30 was held in Belém, Brazil (Pará state, Amazon mouth, November 10-21, 2025) — strategically located in the Amazon rainforest to emphasize deforestation as climate emergency. President Lula positioned Brazil as climate champion despite prior domestic critics of his environmental commitment. Key outcomes: 'Global Mutirão' (Brazilian Portuguese: collective community effort, mutual aid) call uniting humanity in climate action; $1.3 trillion/year climate finance by 2035 (vs COP29's paltry $300B); Tropical Forests Forever Facility (TFFF) launched with $6.7 billion pledged by 7 countries and endorsed by 53 nations; Loss & Damage Fund operationalized with $431.52M (far short of $724B/year need); tripling adaptation finance by 2035. India positioned as Global South voice, demanding equity-based climate action and technology transfer for developing nations. COP31 will be Antalya, Turkey 2026.

question_text: The COP30 Belém 2025 climate finance decision sets a target to mobilise how much per year by 2035?
explanation: COP30 Belém adopted an unprecedented $1.3 trillion/year climate finance target by 2035 — a 4.3x increase over COP29 Baku's New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) of $300 billion/year. India, as lead voice for Global South, had called COP29's $300B 'paltry and inadequate,' arguing that climate damages in developing nations far exceed this (estimated $300-600B/year in adaptation needs alone). COP30's $1.3T target represented a major victory for Indian climate diplomacy and coalition-building with African, ASEAN, and SIDS nations. Financing structure: mitigation (30%), adaptation (50%), loss/damage (20%). COP30 also tripled adaptation finance by 2035 and operationalized the Loss & Damage Fund (FRLD) with initial $431.52M pledged. India positioned itself as leading the 'coalition of the vulnerable' — nations most affected by climate change despite lowest historical emissions.

question_text: The Loss & Damage Fund (FRLD) became operational at COP30. What was its pledged amount as it opened for business?
explanation: FRLD (Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage) became operational at COP30 with $431.52 million pledged — catastrophically short of the estimated $724 billion/year needed to address climate disasters in vulnerable nations. Pledging countries: Germany ($100M), USA ($50M), Denmark, Sweden, Fiji, South Korea, etc. The fund's glacial pace reflects developed-nation reluctance to acknowledge climate reparations as moral/legal obligation. Timeline: FRLD agreed at COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh, Nov 2022), operationalized at COP28 (Dubai, Dec 2023), but opened for actual disbursement only at COP30. India advocated strongly for adequate FRLD funding as part of 'Common But Differentiated Responsibilities' (CBDR+RC) — principle that developed nations bear historical responsibility for emissions and must finance adaptation in developing nations. Small island developing states (SIDS) and LDCs (least developed countries) are FRLD's intended beneficiaries.

question_text: COP30 Belém 2025 Political Package set what target for adaptation finance by 2035?
explanation: COP30 adopted a target to TRIPLE adaptation finance by 2035 — signalling recognition that adaptation (helping countries cope with climate impacts) requires equal or greater priority than mitigation (reducing emissions). Adaptation finance helps developing nations manage climate impacts: extreme flooding (India monsoons), prolonged droughts (Sub-Saharan Africa), sea-level rise (SIDS, Bangladesh), heat waves (South Asia). Current adaptation finance: ~$30-50B/year, funded primarily through bilateral aid rather than multilateral mechanisms. COP29 Baku's $300B NCQG focused heavily on mitigation; COP30's tripling of adaptation represented advocacy victory by India, African nations, and SIDS for climate justice — developed nations caused climate change through historical emissions; developing nations suffer disproportionate impacts without responsibility. India emphasizes this equity gap as core to its G20 2023, BRICS 2024, and COP30 advocacy, positioning India as voice of 'climate vulnerable' nations.

question_text: Which COP was the FIRST to include 'transition away from fossil fuels' language in its final text?
explanation: COP28 Dubai (2023) was the first COP to include explicit 'transition away from fossil fuels' language in its final agreement — a historic breakthrough after nearly 30 years of climate negotiations. COP26 Glasgow (2021) addressed 'phase down,' not phase out. COP27 Sharm el-Sheikh (2022) created Loss & Damage Fund but avoided fossil fuel language due to OPEC opposition. COP28 language was carefully negotiated by UAE (COP host, oil-producing nation): 'transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems' without mandatory timeline, allowing flexibility. COP29 Baku (2024) set $300B/year New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) for climate finance. COP30 Belém (2025) raised climate finance to $1.3T/year by 2035 and tripled adaptation targets. India supported all fossil fuel language while advocating for Just Transition provisions protecting development rights of Global South nations dependent on coal/oil revenue.

question_text: Where will COP31 be held in 2026?
explanation: COP31 will be held in Antalya, Turkey in November 2026 (Australia sharing co-leadership role as Pacific perspective on climate). Turkey's selection reflects NATO alliance, geopolitical centrality (Black Sea, Middle East, Central Asia), and commitment to renewable energy transition (solar/wind capacity growth). COP host sequence: Dubai UAE (COP28, 2023) → Baku Azerbaijan (COP29, 2024) → Belém Brazil (COP30, 2025) → Antalya Turkey (COP31, 2026). India will be active participant in COP31, advancing climate justice demands, Loss & Damage Fund operationalization, and technology transfer mechanisms. After COP30's climate finance victories, COP31 focus likely: implementation mechanisms, Just Transition support, carbon markets (Article 6) finalization, nature-based solutions (NbS) for mitigation. UNFCCC Secretariat HQ: Bonn, Germany. COP process demonstrates Indian diplomatic leadership within Global South climate coalition.

question_text: COP30 significance: Belém is located in which Brazilian state, at the mouth of which river?
explanation: Belém is in Pará state, at the mouth (delta/estuary) of the Amazon River where it meets the Atlantic Ocean. Brazil's President Lula championed Belém as COP30 host to highlight Amazon deforestation threats and biodiversity conservation as core climate issues. The Amazon rainforest is a critical carbon sink: absorbs ~2 billion tons of CO2/year, stores 150-200 gigatons of carbon, home to ~10% of world's species, regulates regional rainfall patterns (supplying water to South American agriculture). Amazon faces tipping point: deforestation + degradation approaching 20-25% threshold beyond which forest converts to savanna (releasing stored carbon and accelerating warming). COP30 in Belém underscored urgency: Amazon protection is non-negotiable for global climate stability. India supports Tropical Forests Forever Facility (TFFF) launched at COP30 as mechanism to finance Amazon protection while respecting Brazil's sovereignty and development rights in Amazon region.

question_text: COP30 'called on' countries to triple adaptation finance. What is the key LIMITATION noted by climate analysts?
option_b: Doesn't specify baseline, funding sources, or target figure
explanation: COP30's call to 'triple adaptation finance by 2035' has critical ambiguities: (1) No baseline specified — 'triple' from what? Current $30-50B/year or different estimate?; (2) No funding sources designated — developed nations, multilateral banks, private sector?; (3) No binding target figure — $90-150B/year is implied but not explicit; (4) No enforcement mechanism — calls are non-binding recommendations. This vagueness, while politically necessary to achieve consensus, weakens implementation. Climate analysts criticized Belém Political Package as emphasizing 'infrastructure of climate action' rather than delivering grand bargain on finance/technology. COP30's real victories: $1.3T global climate finance target (2035), TFFF launch with $6.7B pledged (though far short of Brazil's $125B goal), FRLD operationalization. India negotiated these as victories while acknowledging limitations, positioning itself as leading Global South voice in climate justice while maintaining constructive engagement with developed nations.

question_text: What was the theme of WEF Davos Annual Meeting 2025 (January 20-24, 2025)?
explanation: 'Collaboration for the Intelligent Age' was WEF Davos 2025 theme (55th Annual Meeting, January 20-24, 2025). AI dominated discourse: generative AI, automation, labor displacement, digital governance, tech regulation. Timing symbolically aligned with Trump's inauguration on January 20, coinciding with heightened US-China tech competition, geopolitical fragmentation, and questions about global cooperation feasibility. Davos 2025 attendance: ~2,500+ delegates across business, government, civil society, academia. India participated prominently: IT sector leadership (TCS, Infosys), policy representation on AI governance, climate finance advocacy. WEF theme progression: 2023='Cooperation in Fragmented World' → 2024='Rebuilding Trust' → 2025='Collaboration for Intelligent Age' → 2026='A Spirit of Dialogue.' Each reflects global challenges: fragmentation, trust deficit, AI acceleration, peace/dialogue urgency.

question_text: What was the theme of WEF Davos Annual Meeting 2026 (January 19-23, 2026)?
explanation: 'A Spirit of Dialogue' was WEF Davos 2026 theme (56th Annual Meeting, January 19-23, 2026) — emphasizing urgent need for diplomatic dialogue amid geopolitical tensions (Russia-Ukraine, Iran-Israel-US war, China-Taiwan, India-Pakistan). Record attendance: 60+ heads of state/government, 400+ political leaders, 830+ CEOs, 2,700+ delegates. Key diplomatic moment: Zelenskyy met Trump bilaterally at Davos; both announced US-Ukraine-Russia trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi on January 23, 2026 (mediated by Pakistan). India participated with representation on AI governance, climate finance, development priorities. Theme reflected Davos organizers' perception that fragmentation and distrust had peaked; dialogue/bridge-building became urgent. This contrasted with 2025's 'Collaboration for Intelligent Age' (focused on technology), signalling shift toward conflict resolution and geopolitical de-escalation as central.

question_text: At WEF Davos 2026, which significant Ukraine peace initiative was announced?
option_b: US-Ukraine-Russia trilateral talks to begin in Abu Dhabi January 23
explanation: At Davos 2026 (January 19-23), Zelenskyy met Trump and announced US-Ukraine-Russia trilateral peace talks to begin in Abu Dhabi on January 23, 2026 — with Pakistan as mediator. This signified Trump's peace initiative emphasis and Zelenskyy's willingness to negotiate after 4+ years of war. Abu Dhabi talks focused on ceasefire terms, territorial arrangements, NATO membership status, reparations. Trump subsequently brokered a 3-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire (May 9-11, 2026) with 1,000-prisoner exchanges each side — described as 'potentially the beginning of the end.' India maintained neutrality on Ukraine: critical of unilateral sanctions, opposed NATO expansion into non-aligned space, advocated for dialogue while acknowledging Russian aggression as violation of UN Charter. Davos 2026 signalled shift from military stalemate to negotiation, validating 'Spirit of Dialogue' theme.

question_text: WEF's Future of Jobs Report predicted what fraction of current jobs will change by 2030, with 39% of skills becoming obsolete?
explanation: WEF Future of Jobs Report (2025): 1 in 4 current jobs (25%) will experience significant disruption by 2030; 39% of current skills will become obsolete within 5 years. Primary disruptors: AI/generative AI, automation, green energy transition, digital transformation, remote work normalization. Sectors most disrupted: administrative/clerical (highest displacement), manufacturing, finance, customer service. Counter-trends: healthcare, skilled trades, AI training/governance roles growing. India noted as having acute employment challenges: 12+ million annual workforce entrants competing for jobs with high AI displacement. WEF calls for reskilling initiatives (vocational education, lifelong learning, STEM emphasis) especially in Global South. India prioritizes tech/IT upskilling, coding academies, vocational training expansion to manage AI-driven labor market disruption.

question_text: What happened to the QUAD Leaders' Summit scheduled to be hosted by India in 2025?
option_a: Held successfully in New Delhi in November 2025
option_b: No leaders' summit convened in 2025; rescheduled to 2026 but still not finalised as of May 2026
option_d: Held virtually due to India-Pakistan tensions
explanation: India's 2025 QUAD Chairmanship (USA 2024 → India 2025 → Australia 2026 → Japan 2027) ended WITHOUT a formal leaders' summit — a significant diplomatic setback reflecting Trump's skepticism toward multilateral forums. Trump's return to presidency in January 2025 signalled deprioritization of QUAD as China-containment vehicle; Trump favored bilateral US-China relations and questioned value of QUAD commitments. EAM S. Jaishankar stated (February 2026) the QUAD summit was 'not cancelled' but unscheduled — diplomatic language indicating Trump's lack of enthusiasm. India pivoted to executing QUAD initiatives despite summit absence: MAITRI (maritime training), QUAD-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission (operationalized June 2025), Critical Minerals Initiative, Ports of the Future Forum (Mumbai, Oct 2025). QUAD FM meeting held in New Delhi (March 2026, US Secretary of State Rubio attending) was framed as leaders-level discussion, substituting for formal summit. This demonstrated India's flexibility in advancing QUAD agenda despite diminished Trump administration commitment.

question_text: The 'QUAD-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission' was first operationalised in which month of 2025?
explanation: QUAD-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission was first operationalized in June 2025 — a mechanism placing rotating naval observers from India, USA, Japan, Australia aboard each other's naval vessels to enhance maritime interoperability, surveillance coordination, and real-time intelligence sharing. Observers rotate quarterly, experiencing each nation's naval operations, building trust, and establishing common protocols for Indo-Pacific maritime security. This was a major QUAD deliverable first announced at QUAD Wilmington Summit (September 2024) and prioritized by India's 2025 QUAD Chairmanship. The mission addresses China's naval expansion and grey-zone tactics (coast guard pressure, island-building, fishing-fleet militarization) in South China Sea and Indian Ocean. India led QUAD-at-Sea design, emphasizing respect for UNCLOS, freedom of navigation, and shared maritime interests. Mission represents operational QUAD cooperation advancing despite leadership summit absence.

question_text: The QUAD 'Ports of the Future Partnership' was launched in 2025. Where was the conference hosted?
explanation: QUAD Ports of the Future Partnership was launched at a major transportation/logistics conference in Mumbai, India (October 2025) — coinciding with India's ASEAN engagement and Indo-Pacific connectivity initiatives. The partnership focuses on: port modernization (green shipping, digital cargo tracking), port authority cooperation, maritime trade facilitation, supply-chain resilience against disruptions. India leveraged Mumbai's status as major Arabian Sea port and QUAD node to position itself as logistics hub for Indo-Pacific. QUAD simultaneously launched: Critical Minerals Initiative (2025) addressing supply-chain vulnerabilities for lithium/cobalt/rare earths critical for EV/renewable energy; QUAD STEM Scholarships (50 annual scholarships for Indo-Pacific students at Indian engineering institutions — IIT, NIT — advancing talent development and soft power). These 2025 QUAD initiatives (despite absent leaders' summit) demonstrated India's commitment to converting QUAD into operational framework advancing shared prosperity, maritime security, and technology cooperation.

question_text: MAITRI (Maritime Initiative for Training in the Indo-Pacific) — a QUAD initiative — primarily does what?
option_b: Trains Indo-Pacific partner nation coast guards
explanation: MAITRI (Maritime Initiative for Training in the Indo-Pacific) trains and builds capacity of Indo-Pacific partner nation coast guards to enhance maritime security, law enforcement, and territorial protection. Program features: training workshops, equipment support, intelligence sharing, capacity assessments. Launched at QUAD Wilmington Summit (September 2024); first assessment workshop held 2025 identifying regional capability gaps in maritime domain awareness, maritime law enforcement, counter-piracy, IUU (illegal, unreported, unregulated) fishing suppression. Targets include ASEAN coast guards, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius — nations vulnerable to Chinese maritime coercion (territorial disputes, fishing rights violations, debt-trap infrastructure). India leads MAITRI curriculum development, leveraging Indian Coast Guard's decades of Indo-Pacific operations. QUAD members: India, USA, Japan, Australia. QUAD formed 2007; revived 2017 as dialogue; elevated to leaders' summit level 2021. MAITRI exemplifies QUAD's operational pivot from dialogue to capacity-building delivery.
