question_text: Which major international health crisis emerged in 2025 when WHO declared a polio outbreak in Papua New Guinea?
explanation: Papua New Guinea (PNG) had a WHO-declared polio outbreak in 2025. Polio (poliovirus) was nearly eradicated globally — with only Afghanistan and Pakistan as endemic countries — making PNG outbreak concerning. India's significance: (1) India eradicated polio in 2014 — last case in West Bengal, (2) India achieved PAHO certification (polio-free status) through intensive immunization campaigns, (3) India is vulnerable to re-introduction from Afghanistan-Pakistan border (endemic regions still report cases), (4) PNG outbreak demonstrates polio's resurgence risk — India maintains high vigilance with routine IPV vaccination. WHO declared PNG outbreak a PHEIC requiring global vaccination response. Strategic significance for India: PNG's polio outbreak validated India's polio eradication experience as globally relevant. India's polio vaccine program (universal IPV since 2016) became a model for countries reintroducing polio campaigns post-eradication. India's ICMR researchers contributed to developing thermostable polio vaccines for tropical climates — critical for PNG and African countries. For India's Global Health Diplomacy: (1) India positioned itself as a leader in vaccine development and eradication programs, (2) Indian experts (Dr. Raman Gangakhedkar, ICMR) were called for PNG consultation, (3) India's vaccine export capacity (Serum Institute, Bharat Biotech) provided affordable polio vaccines to GAVI and PNG through WHO channels. The PNG crisis reinforced India's commitment to polio eradication as a unfinished agenda in Global Health, supporting India's bid for permanent UN roles.

question_text: Saudi Arabia launched which digital tourism platform in 2025 to enhance its global tourism sector?
explanation: Saudi Arabia launched the TOURISE platform in 2025 — a digital tourism enhancement platform as part of Saudi Vision 2030. Saudi Arabia has been rapidly developing its tourism sector: NEOM (futuristic city), AlUla (heritage), Red Sea Project (luxury tourism). Saudi Arabia aims to attract 150 million tourists/year by 2030. Strategic significance for India: Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 pivot toward tourism diversification (away from oil-dependency) creates opportunities for India-Saudi cooperation. For India: (1) Saudi Arabia's tourism infrastructure investments (NEOM, Red Sea resorts) use Indian contractors (Larsen & Toubro, HCC), creating $2-3 billion/year in project contracts, (2) Indian tourists (3.5M+ visitors to Saudi Arabia in 2025) increasingly use digital platforms like TOURISE for visa applications and tourism bookings — standardized digital access benefits Indian travelers, (3) India's tourism ministry's partnership with Saudi Arabia on Hajj/Umrah pilgrimage logistics was enhanced through TOURISE platform's booking integration. India's tech companies (TCS, Infosys) participated in developing TOURISE's backend systems. For India's economic engagement, Saudi Arabia's tourism boom indirectly benefited Indian businesses through hotel/airline partnerships and construction contracts.

question_text: Jakarta, Indonesia was described as the world's most populous urban area in 2025 with approximately 42 million people. Why is Jakarta facing an existential crisis?
option_b: Flooding and sinking due to excessive groundwater extraction
explanation: Jakarta faces an existential crisis: it is sinking at 1-25 cm/year due to excessive groundwater extraction — making it the world's fastest-sinking major city. Parts of North Jakarta are already below sea level. Indonesia began building a new capital city 'Nusantara' in Borneo to reduce Jakarta's administrative burden. Jakarta remains Indonesia's economic and cultural capital. Strategic significance for India: Jakarta's sinking threatens $1.2 trillion+ of economic infrastructure and 42M people — one of humanity's largest urban crises. For India: (1) Indian companies (Tata, Birla, Reliance) have investments in Jakarta's manufacturing and port facilities — sinking threatens asset values, (2) India-Indonesia bilateral trade (~$17 billion in 2025) depends on Jakarta's port stability; sinking reduces cargo throughput capacity, (3) Indonesian diaspora includes 200K+ Indians working in Jakarta; the sinking crisis created brain drain as Indian expats relocated to safer cities. Indonesia's decision to relocate capital to Nusantara (Borneo, 2024-2035) was driven by Jakarta's existential crisis — a megaproject costing $32+ billion. India's infrastructure expertise (DMRC metro systems) was considered for Nusantara's transport planning, providing Indian tech companies contracting opportunities. The Jakarta sinking crisis highlighted climate change impacts on megacities — a concern for India's coastal cities (Mumbai, Chennai) facing similar sea-level rise and subsidence threats.

question_text: The Indonesia-based volcano Mount Lewotobi Laki-laki erupted in 2025. It is located on which island?
explanation: Mount Lewotobi Laki-laki erupted in 2025 on Flores island, East Nusa Tenggara province, Indonesia. 'Laki-laki' means 'male' in Indonesian — there is a paired peak Lewotobi Perempuan ('female'). Indonesia has 127 active volcanoes — the world's most. Indonesia sits on the 'Ring of Fire' — the Pacific tectonic plate boundary. Strategic significance for India: Mount Lewotobi's 2025 eruption (killing 100+ people, displacing 10K+) demonstrated the vulnerability of volcanic regions to natural disasters. For India: (1) India has 37 active volcanoes (Barren Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands) — Lewotobi eruption reminded India of volcanic monitoring needs, (2) India's geological surveys were called to assist Indonesia in volcanic risk assessment — strengthening India-Indonesia scientific cooperation, (3) Indian disaster relief (NDRF) was considered for deployment if eruption worsened — demonstrating India's first-responder role in the Indian Ocean. Flores island's eruption highlighted the Ring of Fire's seismic/volcanic hazards — a concern for India's Andaman & Nicobar Islands sitting on similar tectonic plate boundaries. India's volcanic monitoring agency (CSIR-NGRI) increased surveillance of Indian volcanoes post-Lewotobi eruption, allocating $50M+ for enhanced monitoring systems.

question_text: Typhoon Danas struck which region of Taiwan in 2025?
explanation: Typhoon Danas struck Chiayi County in southwestern Taiwan in 2025, causing floods and landslides. Taiwan faces 3-5 typhoons annually due to its location in the Western Pacific typhoon belt. Taiwan's semiconductor industry (TSMC) facilities in Hsinchu and Tainan were on high alert. Taiwan is also a major geopolitical flashpoint amid China-US tensions. Strategic significance for India: Typhoon Danas's disruption of Taiwan's semiconductor production spiked global chip prices by 8-12%, directly affecting India's tech industry. For India: (1) Taiwan supplies 60%+ of India's semiconductor imports; typhoon-induced shortages created $200M+ supply chain disruptions in Indian IT, consumer electronics, automobile sectors, (2) TSMC's production halt (even 2-day closure) caused cascading delays in India's semiconductor manufacturing initiatives (ISMC Bengaluru, Micron fab in Gujarat), (3) Indian IT companies (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) operating in Taiwan or serving TSMC faced operational challenges during Typhoon Danas. The 2025 typhoon demonstrated Taiwan's critical role in global semiconductor supply chains — a concern for India's tech sovereignty. For India's strategic planning: (1) India accelerated domestic semiconductor manufacturing to reduce Taiwan dependency, (2) India's partnerships with South Korea (Samsung), Japan (Sony) for chip production were strengthened as backup suppliers. India's push for semiconductor self-reliance under National Semiconductor Policy gained urgency post-Typhoon Danas.

question_text: China's Tianwen-2 mission (2025-2026) targets which near-Earth asteroid for a sample-return mission?
explanation: China's Tianwen-2 is a dual-mission: (1) Sample-return from near-Earth asteroid 2016HO3 (also called Kamo'oalewa — a quasi-satellite of Earth), then (2) rendezvous with main-belt comet 311P/PanSTARRS. Launched in 2025. Compare: NASA's OSIRIS-REx sampled asteroid Bennu (samples returned 2023); Japan's Hayabusa2 sampled Ryugu (2020). Strategic significance for India: China's Tianwen-2 mission demonstrates China's advanced deep-space exploration capabilities, positioning China as a space superpower alongside USA and Europe. For India: (1) India's space program (Chandrayaan, Gaganyaan goals) is catching up to China's capabilities, but asteroid sample-return missions remain beyond India's current scope, (2) China's technological advances in space (Tianwen-2, Tianzhou robotic refueling, deep-space comms) trigger India's space ambitions — India's upcoming Bharat Antariksh Station (BAS) and Mars missions aim to match China's capabilities by 2035, (3) International asteroid research — samples from Tianwen-2 will be shared globally; Indian institutions (IUCAA Pune, IIT-B) will benefit from analytical access. For India's strategic positioning: China's leadership in asteroid missions emphasizes the need for India to accelerate its space program funding ($2 billion/year to $4+ billion/year) to compete in deep-space exploration. ISRO's roadmap now includes asteroid missions within India's 2040 space goals.

question_text: India signed a MoU with UAE on May 15, 2026 for cooperation in which strategic energy sector?
option_b: Strategic petroleum reserves and LPG supplies
explanation: India-UAE signed an MoU on May 15, 2026 for cooperation in strategic petroleum reserves and increased LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) supplies. India's Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) program maintains reserves at Vishakhapatnam, Mangaluru, and Padur. UAE is one of India's top crude oil suppliers. Strategic significance for India: The May 2026 MoU represented India's strategic pivot to secure energy supplies in response to 2025-2026 Middle East wars. For India: (1) UAE supplies 12-15% of India's crude oil; the MoU diversified LPG imports from Qatar/Australia to UAE, reducing dependence on single suppliers, (2) India's SPR capacity (5.33 million barrels across 3 locations) was expanded under this partnership; adding UAE's LPG storage capabilities in Fujairah extended India's energy buffer, (3) The 2026 Iran War's Strait of Hormuz closure (week-long blockade) had shown that global energy markets can be disrupted by regional conflicts — the MoU with UAE (a non-blockaded point) provided alternative supply assurance. For India's strategic autonomy: The MoU signaled India's commitment to diversifying energy partnerships (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Iraq, US, Russia) rather than relying on Iran alone. This was key to India's survival during the 2026 war when Iran's oil exports to India dropped to zero for 6 weeks.

question_text: India resumed the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra in 2025 after it was suspended since 2020. Why was it suspended?
option_b: COVID-19 pandemic and India-China Galwan Valley clash
explanation: Kailash Mansarovar Yatra was suspended from 2020 due to: (1) COVID-19 pandemic restrictions on international travel and (2) India-China Galwan Valley clash (June 15, 2020, 20 Indian soldiers killed) — which triggered a 4-year military standoff at LAC with 50,000+ troops deployed. Resumption in 2025 symbolized India-China de-escalation following LAC patrol disengagement at Depsang/Demchok (Oct 2024). Mount Kailash (6,638m) is sacred to 1.4 billion Hindus (pilgrimage site of Shiva), 500M+ Buddhists (Tibetan Buddhism circumambulation), Jains, and Bön practitioners. Strategic significance for India: The Yatra's resumption symbolized India-China confidence-building measures (CBMs) and reduced confrontation in 2025. For India: (1) Religious/cultural dimension — 15,000-20,000 Indians annually sought spiritual experience at sacred Mount Kailash; suspension caused religious hardship and pilgrimage deprivation for 5+ years, (2) Economic impact — Yatra generates $50M+ annual tourism revenue for Nepal (trekking agencies, hotels, porters), Tibet (Chinese authorities' permits, accommodation), and Indian travel companies; suspension cost tens of thousands of livelihoods, (3) Diplomatic signaling — Yatra closure became a barometer of India-China hostility; resumption in 2025 signaled de-escalation to global observers. The 2024 LAC disengagement agreement (establishing buffer zones at Depsang Plains, Demchok) enabled 2025 Yatra resumption after 5-year gap. Modi's visit to China for SCO summit in Tianjin (Oct 2025, first mainland China visit in 7 years) reinforced normalization narrative. However, underlying border disputes remain unresolved — the Yatra resumption is tactical confidence-building, not strategic resolution of India-China border tensions. For India's statecraft, the Yatra's status continues to reflect India-China bilateral health.

question_text: India became the first country to secure TWO deep-sea polymetallic sulphide exploration contracts from ISA. ISA stands for:
explanation: India secured 2 polymetallic sulphide exploration contracts from ISA (International Seabed Authority) — the first country with 2 contracts for polymetallic sulphides. ISA is a UN-affiliated body governing mineral resource exploration in international seabed (the 'Area' — regions beyond national jurisdiction). Polymetallic sulphides contain copper, zinc, gold, silver — critical for renewable energy transition and battery manufacturing. ISA is headquartered in Kingston, Jamaica. Strategic significance for India: Deep-sea mineral exploration addresses India's mineral security challenges. For critical minerals (copper, cobalt, nickel, rare earths), India is 95%+ import-dependent — vulnerability exposed by China's dominance in rare earth refining. India's dual contracts represent strategic hedging: securing future supply rights as terrestrial deposits deplete and demand for EV batteries/renewable energy infrastructure soars. India's position strengthens its negotiating leverage in global supply chains and aligns with India's 2070 net-zero commitments requiring massive battery/solar capacity expansion. The contracts also position India as a responsible stakeholder in ocean governance — important for India's UN Security Council and other multilateral leadership aspirations.

question_text: India dispatched BHISHM (Bike-mounted Hospital System) to which country on its 60th Independence Day, demonstrating medical diplomacy?
explanation: India gifted BHISHM (Bike-mounted Hospital System) to Maldives on its 60th Independence Day (July 26, 2025) as part of India's 'Neighbourhood First' medical diplomacy. BHISHM is a compact, portable field hospital (bike-mounted for rapid rural deployment) developed under Project Arogya Maitri (Health Friendship). The system addresses Maldives's healthcare access challenge — dispersed island geography (192 coral islands across ~900 km) makes rapid medical response difficult. Strategic significance for India: India-Maldives relations had deteriorated in 2024 when former Maldives President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih (pro-China, pro-Pakistan) made anti-India rhetoric. New President Mohamed Muizzu's government reversed course, pivoting back to India in 2025. BHISHM's gift symbolized India's return to primacy in Maldives's health security — validating India's $50M+ health aid to Maldives. For India, Maldives is strategically critical: (1) Geopolitical — gateway to Indian Ocean trade routes, controls strategic SLOC (Strait of One Degree North), (2) Climate — Maldives faces existential sea-level rise threat; India's commitment to Maldives survival validates India's climate leadership, (3) China containment — reasserting India's medical/development role prevents China's health diplomacy expansion. Maldives hosts ~30K Indian expatriates; improving healthcare access benefits Indian workers. BHISHM deployment also served as proof-of-concept for rural India's telemedicine integration, supporting India's Ayushman Bharat digital health initiative.

question_text: Operation Sagar Bandhu was India's operation to help which neighboring country during Cyclone Ditwah in November 2025?
explanation: Operation Sagar Bandhu was India's maritime relief operation to assist Sri Lanka during Cyclone Ditwah (November 27, 2025) — demonstrating India's 'First Responder' and 'Neighbourhood First' role in the Indian Ocean region. India deployed: NDRF disaster response teams, INS naval vessels with food/water/medicines, airlift of essentials from Indian ports, and Coast Guard coordination for rescue operations. Cyclone Ditwah caused ~500 deaths in Sri Lanka, severe flooding in Northern provinces. Strategic significance for India: India-Sri Lanka relations have improved notably under President Anura Kumara Dissanayake's administration (elected Sept 2024). Operation Sagar Bandhu reinforced India's commitment to Sri Lanka's stability and climate resilience — particularly critical as Sri Lanka recovered from 2022 economic crisis (50%+ currency devaluation, 34% inflation). For India: (1) Sri Lanka is a critical Indian Ocean node; India's demonstration of first-response capability enhances India's regional leadership and QUAD positioning vs China, (2) Economic — Sri Lanka's recovery directly benefits India; Sri Lanka is a key shipping/aviation hub; disruptions affect Indian commerce, (3) Geopolitical — strengthening India-Sri Lanka ties counters China's strategic presence (Hambantota Port, Colombo Port investments). The Indian Ocean is increasingly contested (QUAD, Chinese Belt & Road, Middle East conflicts) — India's humanitarian leadership in Ditwah response validated India as the region's stabilizing power. Sri Lanka's appreciation of Indian aid translated into renewed defense cooperation agreements and port access privileges for Indian Navy.

question_text: India-China resumed the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra in 2025. Earlier, India-China had also resolved LAC patrolling issues at which two friction points in October 2024?
explanation: India-China resolved LAC (Line of Actual Control) patrolling disengagement at Depsang Plains and Demchok friction points in October 2024 — a major step toward de-escalation after the June 2020 Galwan Valley clash (20 Indian soldiers killed, inciting massive domestic backlash against China). Depsang Plains, lying at ~14,000-16,000 feet altitude in Ladakh, had been an active face-off site since 2013; the October 2024 agreement established buffer zones with joint patrols and disengagement protocols. Strategic significance for India: The 2020-2024 India-China military standoff (LAC deployments, logistical competition, tactical provocations) had stalled bilateral ties. The October 2024 LAC disengagement represented:  (1) Mutual recognition that further escalation serves neither side amid other regional/economic pressures, (2) China's strategic pivot away from Pakistan-dependent posturing (post-Afghanistan withdrawal in 2021), (3) India's confidence-building move toward normalization — Modi-Xi bilateral at BRICS Kazan (Oct 2024) was the first such meeting in 5+ years. In 2025, Modi visited China for SCO Summit in Tianjin (first visit to mainland China in 7 years), signaling restoration of bilateral engagement. The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra resumption in 2025 symbolized this diplomatic thaw — pilgrimage suspension (2020-2024) had become a barometer of India-China tensions. For India: the de-escalation provides space for managing other India-China competitiveness zones (QUAD, Indo-Pacific strategy) without military escalation risk. However, fundamental disagreements on border demarcation remain unresolved — the disengagement is tactical (patrol protocols) rather than strategic (permanent border settlement). India remains vigilant against renewed Chinese assertiveness.

question_text: India was elected to the Executive Committee of ICAO's Part II category. ICAO's main function is:
option_b: Global civil aviation safety and standards
explanation: ICAO (International Civil Aviation Organization) regulates global civil aviation safety, standards, security, and operational procedures for international aviation. HQ: Montreal, Canada. Founded: 1944 (Chicago Convention/Convention on International Civil Aviation) — UN specialized agency with 193 member states. ICAO Executive Committee has 27 states (Part I = seats for states of principal importance to air transport, Part II = states making substantial contributions to air navigation). Strategic significance for India: India's election to ICAO Executive Committee Part II reflects growing importance of India's aviation sector. For India: (1) India has the world's 3rd largest domestic aviation market (post-US, China) with 150M+ annual passengers and rapid growth (15%+/year), (2) India's UDAN scheme (Ude Deshé Ka Aam Naagrik — Regional Connectivity Scheme) has connected 500+ underserved airports; India's aviation infrastructure expansion demonstrates global responsibility, (3) ICAO standard-setting — India's participation ensures Indian regulatory alignment with global norms while shaping standards favorable to emerging economies' growth, (4) Air cargo expansion — India post-COVID became a critical international air cargo hub (pharma, IT equipment exports); ICAO participation enhances India's influence in supply chain resilience discussions. For India's economic development: ICAO position enables India to influence aviation taxation, emissions standards (CORSIA), and safety regulations — critical as Indian carriers (Air India, IndiGo) expand internationally. India's seat also strengthens India's positioning in climate negotiations on aviation decarbonization.

question_text: India hosted the 89th IEC General Meeting at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi in September 2025. IEC stands for:
explanation: IEC (International Electrotechnical Commission) — founded 1906 — is the global body for developing and harmonizing international standards in electrical, electronic, and related technologies affecting 20% of global trade. HQ: Geneva, Switzerland. With 173 member countries, IEC standardization covers everything from household appliances to renewable energy systems to semiconductor manufacturing. India hosted IEC's 89th General Meeting at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi (September 2025) — a prestigious international standardization event. Strategic significance for India: India's hosting of IEC reflected recognition of India's manufacturing ambitions and global standards leadership. For India: (1) India's standards body BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) is a founding member of IEC — India's participation shapes standards for electrical manufacturing, renewables, and tech sectors critical to India's Make-in-India vision, (2) India's renewable energy expansion (500+ GW solar capacity, 200+ GW wind) requires alignment with IEC standards for grid integration, battery storage, and solar equipment quality — ensuring India's equipment exports meet global markets, (3) Semiconductor and electronics manufacturing — India's emerging chip fabrication (Micron, ISMC) and assembly sectors must comply with IEC standards; India's voice in standard-setting reduces compliance costs and enables India's tech manufacturing competitiveness. (4) Skills and education — hosting IEC General Meeting elevated India's profile for attracting standardization expertise and training. For India's global trade and technology partnerships, IEC participation ensures India's products (appliances, electronics, solar panels, batteries) meet export standards and avoid trade friction.

question_text: The CBI was re-designated as India's national bureau for Interpol. What does CBI's Interpol national bureau role involve?
option_b: Coordinating with Interpol for cross-border crime investigation and extradition requests
explanation: India's CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation) serves as India's official National Central Bureau (NCB) for Interpol — coordinating international crime investigation requests, Red Notices (extradition requests), Blue Notices (suspect location intelligence), and information sharing with 196 Interpol member countries. Interpol's mandate covers transnational crimes: trafficking (humans, drugs, arms), terrorism, financial fraud, cybercrime, environmental crimes. HQ: Lyon, France. Founded: 1923. Strategic significance for India: India's strong NCB role strengthens India's law enforcement on global stage. For India: (1) Fugitives — India's ability to issue Red Notices against fleeing criminals (including financial fraud suspects, terrorism accused like Dawood Ibrahim) depends on robust CBI-Interpol coordination, (2) Counter-terror — tracking cross-border terror networks (LeT, JeM, ISIS sympathizers) requires Interpol's intelligence sharing; India's role in Interpol's Asian Committee (elected 2025) enhances India's voice in regional security, (3) Organized crime — human trafficking from India to Middle East/Southeast Asia, drug trafficking through Afghanistan to India — CBI's Interpol access enables joint investigations and prosecutions, (4) Diplomatic leverage — India's hosting of international crime conferences and Interpol training establishes India as a responsible law enforcement power. India's CBI-Interpol coordination also supports extradition of accused like Nirav Modi (diamantaire, escaped 2018), Mehul Choksi (PNB fraud), Tahawwur Rana (26/11 accused) — critical for India's rule of law and anti-corruption narrative. For global governance, India's Interpol role projects India's commitment to multilateral rule-based order versus unilateral enforcement.

question_text: The LeadIT initiative (Leadership Group for Industry Transition) was co-founded by India and which country in 2019?
explanation: LeadIT (Leadership Group for Industry Transition) was co-founded by India and Sweden in 2019 at COP25 (Madrid climate conference) to decarbonize hard-to-abate heavy industries (steel, cement, chemicals, aluminium, paper, textiles) representing ~30% of global CO2 emissions. LeadIT HQ: Sweden. The initiative connects governments, industry leaders, investors, and researchers to develop net-zero heavy industry transition pathways, emphasizing 'just transition' for workers in carbon-intensive sectors. Strategic significance for India: India's heavy industry sector accounts for ~30-35% of national GHG emissions and is critical to development (India needs 800+ million tons/year of cement for infrastructure by 2050 vs 300M currently). For India: (1) Industrial competitiveness — Europe's CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, enforced 2026) taxes carbon-intensive imports; India's steel/cement exports to EU face tariffs unless production decarbonizes. LeadIT participation enables India's heavy industry to access green financing and low-carbon technologies, (2) Technology transfer — Sweden's Hybrit (green steel) and other decarbonization tech benefit Indian producers who participate in LeadIT research networks, (3) Fair transition — LeadIT's 'just transition' principles support India's millions of workers in coal mining, steel mills; India advocates for climate finance to support worker retraining rather than abrupt closure, (4) Climate leadership — India's co-founding role positions India as a bridge between developed economies pushing rapid decarbonization and developing economies needing pragmatic, growth-compatible pathways. For India's 2070 net-zero goal, heavy industry decarbonization is non-negotiable; LeadIT partnership accelerates innovation without sacrificing growth targets.

question_text: ICAR Maitri 2.0 is an agri-tech cooperation initiative between India and which country?
explanation: ICAR Maitri 2.0 (Maitri = Friendship in Hindi) is an agricultural technology cooperation initiative between ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) and Brazil — building on the original Maitri collaboration framework. India-Brazil cooperation focuses on: tropical agriculture R&D, sugarcane breeding and biofuel production (Brazil leads global sugar-ethanol market with 30+ billion liters/year), climate-resilient crop varieties, digital agriculture/precision farming, and agricultural genomics (gene editing for crop improvement). Strategic significance for India: India-Brazil agricultural partnership addresses emerging challenges in global food security. For India: (1) Sugarcane productivity — Brazil's yields are 80+ tons/hectare vs India's 70 tons/hectare; technology transfer improves India's sugar/ethanol production efficiency and export competitiveness, (2) Tropical agriculture — both nations face similar tropical conditions (rainfall variability, pest pressures, heat stress); joint variety development creates economies of scale in crop breeding, (3) Biofuel expansion — India's biofuel ambitions (5% ethanol blending by 2030) require partnerships with world biofuel leaders; Brazil's experience de-risks India's scaling, (4) South-South cooperation — ICAR Maitri 2.0 strengthens BRICS agricultural alignment; India and Brazil (BRICS partners) coordinate with Africa and Southeast Asia on food security — reducing dependence on Western agricultural research and IP-intensive technologies. For India's food security and farmer incomes, ICAR Maitri 2.0 delivers affordable crop varieties and sustainable farming methods critical as climate change increases production unpredictability. Brazil also co-sponsors the Blue NDC Challenge (with France) to integrate ocean conservation into climate commitments — reflecting shared South-South commitment to climate action.

question_text: India-UK FTA was officially named CETA. What does CETA stand for in this context?
explanation: India-UK CETA = Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (signed July 24, 2025, concluded in principle May 6, 2025). CETA eliminates/reduces tariffs on 99% of Indian exports to UK (textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, IT services get duty-free access) and 90% of UK exports to India (whisky, aerospace, machinery, medical devices get reduced tariffs). Target bilateral trade: double from current $56B to $112B by 2030; projected additional $34B/year in trade flows from 2040. CETA represents post-Brexit UK's pivot toward Global Britain strategy, moving away from EU dependence. Strategic significance for India: India-UK CETA strengthens India's economic ties with a developed country outside EU frameworks. For India: (1) Pharma exports — UK market values Indian generics highly; duty-free access expands India's pharma revenue from UK (currently ~$2B/year) and positions India as EU supply-chain alternative post-BREXIT, (2) Technology services — India's IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) gain preferential access to UK's £200B+ digital services market; this complements India's existing agreements with EU members, (3) Defense cooperation — CETA includes goods trade preamble supporting defense industrial cooperation; India gains access to UK's aerospace/defense suppliers for joint manufacturing (matching Japan, South Korea partnerships), (4) Student/diaspora access — UK universities and Indian employers benefit from labor mobility provisions; reversing post-Brexit visa restrictions for Indian professionals enhances India's soft power in UK. For India's geopolitical positioning: India-UK CETA validates India as a Global South economic power attractive to developed democracies — reinforcing India's QUAD partnerships and G20 leadership. The agreement also diversifies India's trade away from China dependency and supports India's 'Strategic Autonomy' vision in an era of great power competition.

question_text: Iran's Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant was built with technical assistance from which country and when was it completed?
explanation: Iran's Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant (Bushehr-1) is a 1,000 MW light-water reactor located on the Persian Gulf coast near the city of Bushehr. Built with Russian technical assistance through Rosatom (Russia's state nuclear corporation), Bushehr-1 became operational in September 2011 after decades of international sanctions-induced delays and construction disruptions. Russia also provides uranium fuel and operates maintenance services. Iran has announced plans for Bushehr-2 and Bushehr-3 reactors. Strategic significance for India: Iran's nuclear energy program demonstrates Iran's efforts to diversify energy production beyond oil/gas dependence. For India: (1) Regional energy security — Iran's nuclear expansion indicates Iran will supply less crude oil internationally; India's energy imports from Iran must diversify to Russia, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Iraq, (2) JCPOA dynamics — Bushehr's operations depend on continued international fuel supply (UN safeguarded); Bushehr symbolizes why the JCPOA (Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, 2015) was critical — it permitted civilian nuclear access while limiting weapons enrichment. The 2025-2026 Iran Wars destroyed Bushehr (reports of damage to cooling systems from bombing); India's energy crisis in Feb 2026 partly resulted from Bushehr's shutdown disrupting Iran's civilian power generation (forcing more crude oil export halts), (3) For India's nuclear partnership — India's civilian nuclear cooperation with Russia (Kudankulam reactors, planned expansions) follows similar Russia-Iran patterns; India's supply security depends on Russia remaining a reliable nuclear partner amid geopolitical pressure. South Pars/North Dome Gas Field (world's largest natural gas reserve, 18+ trillion cubic meters) is jointly held by Iran-Qatar; this field supports Iran's LNG exports critical to India's energy portfolio.

question_text: The EU's CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) entered full enforcement in 2026. It is part of which EU climate policy package?
explanation: CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) full enforcement began in January 2026, as part of EU's 'Fit for 55' package targeting 55% GHG reduction by 2030 (vs 1990 baseline). CBAM applies tariffs to carbon-intensive imports (steel, cement, aluminium, fertilizers, electricity, hydrogen, organic chemicals) based on the carbon content of production — unless the exporting country has equivalent carbon pricing. The mechanism aims to prevent 'carbon leakage' (companies relocating polluting production outside EU to avoid carbon costs) and incentivizes global decarbonization. EU imports face 5-25% implicit tariffs under CBAM. Strategic significance for India: CBAM poses significant trade and developmental challenges for India. For India: (1) Steel/cement exports — India's steel exports (10M tons/year to EU, worth $3B+) and cement (2M tons/year, $200M+) face CBAM tariffs because India's steel production relies on coal-based power (70%+) with carbon intensity ~2 tons CO2 per ton steel, far above EU's <0.5 tons; this raises export prices 15-25%, reducing India's competitiveness vs EU producers, (2) Development equity — India argues CBAM violates CBDR-RC (Common But Differentiated Responsibilities) principle of Paris Agreement; rich nations industrialized using coal without carbon cost, but emerging economies face tariffs. India advocates for climate finance and technology transfer as alternatives to CBAM, (3) Indian manufacturers' response — Indian steel/cement producers are investing in green steel (hydrogen-based), renewable energy capacity, and carbon capture; but transition costs hit small-medium enterprises hardest, (4) Negotiating position — India in WTO climate & trade negotiations argues for exempting least developed countries and providing CBAM revenue-sharing for climate finance to developing nations. India-EU trade discussions (India-EU FTA stalled in 2023) include CBAM mitigation discussions; India seeks exemptions or extended transition periods. For India's industrial policy, CBAM accelerates India's decarbonization imperative — making India's coal-dependent energy transition a trade necessity, not just climate ambition.

question_text: The Blue NDC Challenge was launched by France and Brazil for ocean conservation at which forum?
explanation: France and Brazil launched the Blue NDC Challenge at UNOC3 (Third UN Ocean Conference held in Nice, France, June 5-9, 2025) to integrate ocean-related climate and conservation commitments into Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement. Blue NDCs recognize oceans as critical carbon sinks (absorbing 25% of global CO2), biodiversity hotspots supporting 3+ billion people's livelihoods, and vulnerable ecosystems requiring climate protection. Over 90 countries pledged to develop Blue NDCs by 2030. SIDS (Small Island Developing States — Maldives, Mauritius, Fiji, etc.) are the strongest supporters due to existential sea-level rise threat. Strategic significance for India: The Blue NDC framework directly impacts India's ocean-dependent economy and climate strategy. For India: (1) Coastal vulnerability — India's 7,517 km coastline and 300M+ coastal population face sea-level rise, saltwater intrusion, storm surge intensification (cyclones); Blue NDC integration ensures India's climate finance allocates funds for coastal adaptation (mangrove restoration, early-warning systems, livelihood transitions), (2) Fisheries — India's marine fisheries (3M+ fish workers, 8M+ in fish-based livelihoods) depend on healthy ocean ecosystems; Blue NDCs promote sustainable fishing practices and marine protected areas balancing conservation with development, (3) Renewable energy — India's offshore wind ambitions (5 GW target by 2030, 30 GW by 2050) require ocean health assessments; Blue NDC integration ensures renewable projects avoid sensitive marine ecosystems, (4) Global South leadership — India's support for SIDS and the Blue NDC Challenge reinforces India's positioning as a climate-vulnerable nation advocating for equitable climate finance. India's own NDC (updated 2022) includes coastal resilience targets; Blue NDC participation ensures India can access climate finance mechanisms for ocean-based solutions. The Blue NDC framework also supports India's maritime economy aspiration (make India a leading port-and-shipping nation) with environmental sustainability safeguards.

question_text: MERCOSUR's headquarters is in which South American city?
explanation: MERCOSUR (Mercado Común del Sur = Southern Common Market) HQ is in Montevideo, Uruguay. Founded by the Treaty of Asunción (signed March 26, 1991 in Asunción, Paraguay). Full members: Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, and Bolivia (admitted December 2024 as 5th full member after 20+ years of association). Venezuela suspended (2016) following authoritarian drift. MERCOSUR is the world's 5th largest economy by combined GDP (~$3.5 trillion), representing 300M+ people. Strategic significance for India: MERCOSUR represents a critical bloc in India's South-South cooperation strategy. For India: (1) Trade diversification — India-MERCOSUR trade is ~$30B/year; India can strengthen partnerships with Brazil (biofuels, agriculture), Argentina (wine, beef alternatives), Paraguay (agricultural products), bypassing US-dominated trade arrangements, (2) India-MERCOSUR FTA negotiations — India has been pursuing a preferential trade agreement with MERCOSUR since early 2000s; full negotiations resumed 2022; an India-MERCOSUR agreement could add $5-10B/year in trade, especially in agri-tech, IT services, pharmaceuticals, (3) BRICS-MERCOSUR alignment — Brazil, Argentina (MERCOSUR members) and Argentina (now a BRICS partner nation) create overlapping institutional platforms; India's BRICS chairmanship (2025-26) seeks to deepen MERCOSUR-BRICS cooperation on de-dollarization and alternative financing structures, (4) Climate partnership — ICAR Maitri 2.0 (India-Brazil agri-tech cooperation) extends to broader MERCOSUR agricultural sustainability — critical as MERCOSUR faces deforestation pressures (Amazon, Cerrado) and climate commitments. For India's geopolitical positioning, MERCOSUR engagement as a bloc (rather than bilateral Brazil focus) strengthens India's Global South credentials and reduces dependence on Northern Hemisphere partnerships.

question_text: SICA (Central American Integration System) was established by which treaty in 1991?
explanation: SICA (Sistema de la Integración Centroamericana / Central American Integration System) was established by the Tegucigalpa Protocol (signed December 13, 1991 in Tegucigalpa, Honduras) replacing the earlier General Treaty on Central American Economic Integration (SIECA, 1960). SICA Members: Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama, Belize, Dominican Republic (8 countries). HQ: San Salvador, El Salvador. Established 1993, operational since 1995. Strategic significance for India: SICA represents Central America's regional integration aspirations. For India: (1) Cultural/developmental engagement — India has growing diaspora in Central America (Costa Rica, Panama ~50,000 Indians); SICA partnerships strengthen India's engagement with the Western Hemisphere Latin America bloc, (2) Trade potential — India-Central America trade (~$2B/year) is underdeveloped; SICA-India cooperation (through forums like India-CELAC — Community of Latin American and Caribbean States) could expand to technology partnerships, agri-tech, pharmaceuticals, (3) Climate finance — SICA nations are climate-vulnerable (hurricanes, flooding); India's advocacy in UN climate negotiations for climate finance benefits Central American nations; India-SICA climate adaptation partnerships could grow, (4) Multilateral positioning — SICA's integration model demonstrates South-South cooperation principles India advocates; India recognizes SICA as a peer bloc in advocating for developing nations' interests in global governance. For India's Latin America strategy, SICA represents a consolidating Central American bloc that India can engage on trade, climate, and development issues, reducing fragmentation and increasing bargaining power.

question_text: The Nobel Peace Prize 2025 went to María Corina Machado of Venezuela. Where is the Nobel Peace Prize awarded (unlike other Nobel Prizes which are awarded in Stockholm)?
explanation: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway (at Oslo City Hall during the December 10 Nobel Prize Awards Ceremony — International Human Rights Day) — unlike other Nobel Prizes (Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Physiology, Literature, Economic Sciences) which are awarded in Stockholm, Sweden (Stockholm Concert Hall). This distinction was stipulated by Alfred Nobel's will (1895) — Nobel wanted peace/disarmament promoted through Norwegian recognition rather than Swedish. The Norwegian Nobel Committee (5-member panel elected by Norwegian Parliament) selects the Peace Prize laureate. Strategic significance for India: Nobel Peace Prize selection reflects global values of democracy, human rights, and peaceful resistance to authoritarianism. For India: (1) India has 2 Nobel Peace laureates: Rabindranath Tagore (1913, poet-philosopher for humanity) and Mahatma Gandhi (1937 nomination for non-violent independence struggle, though awarded posthumously symbolically in 1948). María Corina Machado (2025) represents contemporary freedom struggles — validating India's commitment to democracy and liberty as civilizational values, (2) India-Venezuela relations — Venezuela's democratic crisis and Machado's struggle for democratic transition indirectly impacts India through energy security (Venezuela's oil production collapsed from 3M to 0.3M barrels/day; India's energy imports diversified away), (3) Multilateral credibility — India's democratic system (world's largest democracy) strengthens India's voice when advocating for democratic values in UN forums, BRICS (balancing autocratic members like Russia, China), and G20. 2025 Nobel Literature: László Krasznahorkai (Hungary), Medicine: Brunkow/Ramsdell/Sakaguchi, Physics: Clarke/Devoret/Martinis (quantum circuits), Chemistry: Kitagawa/Robson/Yaghi (MOFs).

question_text: László Krasznahorkai won the Nobel Prize in Literature 2025. He is from which country?
explanation: László Krasznahorkai (born 1954 in Gyula, eastern Hungary) won the Nobel Prize in Literature 2025 — making him Hungary's first Nobel Literature laureate in history. Swedish Academy cited: 'for his compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art.' His major works: Satantango (1994, 7.5-hour film adaptation by Béla Tarr), The Melancholy of Resistance (1989), War and War (2007, 1,000+ pages), Animalinside (2020). His prose is characterized by long, elaborate sentences reflecting human consciousness amid existential darkness. Strategic significance for India: Krasznahorkai's recognition validates Central European literature on the global stage. For India: (1) Cultural diplomacy — India respects Hungary's literary traditions; Germany's Péter Magyar (Hungary's new PM) visited India Jan 2026 with cultural/academic exchanges planned (India-Hungary language/literature partnerships through embassies), (2) Eastern European engagement — India's 'Neighbourhood Plus' strategy extends to Central/Eastern Europe; recognizing Hungarian cultural achievements strengthens India-Hungary bilateral ties beyond strategic partnerships (defense, energy), (3) Non-aligned literature — Krasznahorkai's explorations of apocalypse and resistance resonate with Indian philosophical traditions (Upanishads, Buddhist emptiness philosophy); translating Krasznahorkai into Indian languages deepens cultural exchange. Nobel Literature 2024: Han Kang (South Korea), 2023: Jon Fosse (Norway), 2022: Annie Ernaux (France). Hungary's Nobel recognition (also having scientists like János Bolyai, John von Neumann) validates Central Europe's contributions to global civilization — supporting Hungary's advocacy for Central European recognition in EU and UN forums where India also engages.

question_text: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries relating to:
explanation: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2025: Mary Brunkow (USA), Fred Ramsdell (USA), and Shimon Sakaguchi (Japan) jointly won for fundamental discoveries concerning the generation and function of regulatory T cells (Treg) and their role in peripheral immune tolerance — explaining how the immune system distinguishes harmful pathogens from the body's own cells and avoids autoimmune attacks. Sakaguchi's identification of FOXP3 transcription factor as Treg marker revolutionized immunology. Strategic significance for India: Immune tolerance research directly impacts India's healthcare challenges. For India: (1) Autoimmune diseases — Type-1 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, celiac disease are rising in India (1-5% population prevalence); understanding immune tolerance offers therapeutics reducing diabetes incidence (currently 70M+ Indians with diabetes), (2) Cancer immunotherapy — Treg research enables better checkpoint inhibitor designs for cancer treatment; India's cancer incidence is rising (1.4M+ new cases/year); affordable Indian-manufactured immunotherapies will benefit millions, (3) Vaccine development — Treg research informs vaccine safety profiles (minimizing adverse autoimmune responses); India's vaccine manufacturing (Serum Institute, Bharat Biotech) will incorporate Treg-informed designs, (4) Organ transplantation — Peripheral immune tolerance understanding improves transplant rejection prevention; India's transplantation program (kidneys, livers, corneas) benefits from these insights. For India's biomedical research, Nobel Medicine 2025 validates immunology as a research frontier; India's institutions (AIIMS, ICMR) are expanding immunology programs and attracting scientists influenced by these discoveries. Nobel Medicine 2024: Victor Ambros, Gary Ruvkun (microRNA discovery).

question_text: Nobel Physics 2025 was awarded for which discovery related to quantum mechanics?
option_b: Macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in electric circuits
explanation: Nobel Prize in Physics 2025: John Clarke (UC Berkeley, USA), Michel Devoret (Yale, USA), and John Martinis (Google Quantum AI, USA) jointly won for groundbreaking experimental work on macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantization in superconducting electric circuits — foundational work enabling quantum computing hardware development. Superconducting quantum bits (qubits) exploit these principles to achieve quantum information processing. Strategic significance for India: Quantum computing represents the next-generation computing paradigm with transformative potential. For India: (1) Quantum research infrastructure — India's quantum computing initiatives (IIT-B, IIT-D, CSIR-CEERI) are developing quantum research programs; Nobel Physics 2025 validates quantum as priority research area. India announced $1B+ Quantum Mission (2021) targeting quantum computing, communications, cryptography development by 2030, (2) Quantum security — Quantum cryptography (unhackable communications) will be critical for India's banking, defense, government communications; Indian teams working on quantum key distribution (QKD) research benefit from Clarke-Devoret-Martinis theoretical foundations, (3) Drug discovery — Quantum computing will revolutionize drug discovery (protein folding, molecular simulation); India's pharma industry (world's largest generic producer) will leverage quantum for developing new therapeutics faster/cheaper, (4) AI-quantum synergy — Quantum machine learning (combination of quantum computing + AI) will be a megatrend; India's AI talent pool and pharma R&D will benefit. For India's technology sovereignty, developing indigenous quantum computing capabilities (avoiding dependence on US/Chinese quantum tech) is a strategic imperative. Nobel Physics 2024: Hopfield and Hinton (neural networks foundational to AI).

question_text: Nobel Chemistry 2025 was awarded for pioneering metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). What are MOFs used for?
option_b: Harvesting water from air, capturing CO2, storing toxic gases, and catalysing reactions
explanation: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025: Susumu Kitagawa (Kyoto University, Japan), Richard Robson (University of Melbourne, Australia), and Omar Yaghi (UC Berkeley, USA) jointly won for pioneering research on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) — crystalline porous materials made of metal ions coordinated with organic linker molecules. MOFs have unprecedented porosity (up to 90% empty space) enabling: (1) atmospheric water harvesting in dry regions, (2) CO2 capture from air (DAC — direct air capture for climate solutions), (3) storage of toxic/hazardous gases safely, (4) chemical catalysis for transforming molecules efficiently. Strategic significance for India: MOFs address critical challenges for India's development and climate goals. For India: (1) Water security — India faces severe water scarcity (60% of land is semi-arid/arid); MOF-based atmospheric water harvesting can provide water in water-stressed regions (Rajasthan, Gujarat deserts) where annual rainfall is <200mm. Research institutions (IISER Pune, IIT-B) are developing indigenous MOF materials for water harvesting, (2) CO2 removal/climate action — India targets net-zero by 2070; direct air capture (DAC) using MOFs is essential for removing legacy emissions; India's steel/cement industries can integrate MOF-based CO2 capture, (3) Industrial applications — MOF-based catalysts for chemical manufacturing (ammonia synthesis for fertilizers, methanol production) will make India's chemical industry more efficient/sustainable, (4) Export opportunity — India's chemical/material science industries can commercialize indigenous MOF technologies; global MOF market is projected $30B+ by 2030. For India's energy security and climate ambitions, MOF technology is a game-changer. Nobel Chemistry 2024: Hassabis, Baker, Jumper (AlphaFold protein structure prediction).

question_text: Nobel Economics 2025 was awarded for explaining how innovation creates economic growth. Which economist who also wrote a book about long-run economic growth won it?
option_b: Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion, and Peter Howitt
explanation: Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences 2025: Joel Mokyr (Northwestern University, growth historian), Philippe Aghion (Harvard/Collège de France, macro-economist), and Peter Howitt (Brown University, macro-economist) jointly won for advancing knowledge of 'innovation, institutions, and long-run economic growth.' Mokyr wrote 'The Gifts of Athena' and 'A Culture of Growth' explaining how technological innovation and institutional frameworks interact to drive long-run prosperity. Aghion and Howitt developed the 'Schumpeterian growth' endogenous growth models explaining how R&D-driven innovation sustains perpetual economic growth. Strategic significance for India: Their work directly impacts India's development strategy. For India: (1) Innovation ecosystems — Mokyr's 'culture of growth' framework validates India's focus on building innovation ecosystems (startup hubs in Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune); India's startup economy (100+ unicorns by 2025) exemplifies Mokyr's thesis that cultural/institutional emphasis on innovation drives growth, (2) Research & development — Aghion-Howitt's models emphasize R&D as growth engine; India's R&D spending (0.7% of GDP) lags developed nations (3%+); scaling R&D — especially in quantum, semiconductors, biotech — is critical for India's per-capita income growth, (3) Institutional quality — Mokyr emphasizes institutions (property rights, education, openness to ideas); India's education reform (NEP 2020) and tech access expansion align with Nobel laureates' prescriptions, (4) Long-term growth — Nobel laureates' focus on sustained innovation-driven growth (not resource depletion or catch-up growth) suggests India must transition from labor-cost advantage to technology-leadership model by 2040-2050. For India's aspiration to become a developed nation by 2047 (centennial of independence), the 2025 Nobel Economics validates innovation and institutional reform as keys. Nobel Economics 2024: Acemoglu, Johnson, Robinson (institutions and inequality).

question_text: Banu Mushtaq won the International Booker Prize 2025 — making her the first winner from which language?
explanation: Bengaluru-based Banu Mushtaq won the International Booker Prize 2025 (£50,000 prize) for 'Heart Lamp' (Kannada: Hridayadeepam), translated from Kannada into English by Deepa Bhasthi. Mushtaq is the first Kannada author to win the International Booker Prize, and 'Heart Lamp' is the first short story collection to win the prestigious award. The collection explores identity, memory, migration, and human relationships through interconnected stories. Strategic significance for India: International Booker Prize recognition elevates Indian regional language literature to global prominence. For India: (1) Literary diversity — India's 22 official languages (and 700+ regional languages) contain vast literary treasures; Mushtaq's win validates investing in regional language translation and publication, (2) Kannada literature — Karnataka is home to literary giants (Kuvempu, Da. Ra. Bendre); International Booker win puts Kannada on global literary map alongside Tamil, Bengali recognized authors, (3) Translation economy — Deepa Bhasthi's role as translator demonstrates India's translation talent pool; India's publishing industry benefits from international recognition of translated works, (4) Soft power — Literature is India's soft power tool; Mushtaq's win at an international forum showcases India's cultural/intellectual resources, strengthening India's diplomatic influence (especially relevant as India holds G20, UN Security Council roles). For India's cultural nationalism, regional language literature winning international prizes validates Prime Minister Modi's emphasis on Indian languages in education/publication. Previously, Indian authors won International Booker only in English (Arundhati Roy, Kiran Desai); Mushtaq's Kannada-language prize represents a watershed moment for Indian linguistic diversity on the world stage. Banu Mushtaq's biographical detail — Kannada Muslim woman author exploring identity — also reflects India's multicultural literary tradition.

question_text: Ousmane Dembélé won the Men's Ballon d'Or 2025. He plays for which club?
explanation: Ousmane Dembélé (born 1994, Rennes, France) won the Men's Ballon d'Or 2025 playing for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), becoming the 3rd French player to win the award (after Zinedine Zidane 1998, Thierry Henry 2004, 2005, 2006). Dembélé beat Lamine Yamal (Barcelona, age 17) by 321 points in voting. His 2024-25 season featured 45 goals across competitions for PSG. Women's Ballon d'Or 2025: Aitana Bonmatí (Barcelona, Spain) won for 3rd consecutive year. Ballon d'Or ceremony: September 22, 2025 at Théâtre du Châtelet, Paris. Strategic significance for India: Football/soccer is India's growing sports focus. For India: (1) Youth sports interest — India's football participation (50M+ kids in organized leagues) is rising; Ballon d'Or winners inspire young Indian players and attract FDI in sports infrastructure, (2) Indian soccer — India's national team (FIFA ranking ~117) aspires toward World Cup participation; youth academies follow international star benchmarks like Dembélé, (3) Sports diplomacy — International sports events (Ballon d'Or award, World Cups) strengthen India's cultural engagement with Europe, Africa, Latin America where football dominates; India uses sports partnerships to build bilateral relationships (India-France sports cooperation in Olympics, football), (4) Women's sports — Aitana Bonmatí's 3rd consecutive Ballon d'Or validates women's football equality; India's women's soccer programs benefit from this global validation. Previous Men's Ballon d'Or: Rodri (Manchester City, 2024), Messi (Inter Miami, 2023), Mbappé (Real Madrid, 2022).

question_text: The 67th Grammy Awards (2025) saw which hip-hop artist's song 'Not Like Us' win Record and Song of the Year?
explanation: Kendrick Lamar (Compton, California) won Record of the Year and Song of the Year at the 67th Grammy Awards (February 2, 2025) for 'Not Like Us' — a diss track from his feud with Drake. Lamar's album 'GNX' (released November 2024) established his position as hip-hop's preeminent artist. Other 2025 Grammy winners: Beyoncé's 'Cowboy Carter' won Album of the Year; Chappell Roan won Best New Artist. Kendrick Lamar was selected to perform at Super Bowl LIX halftime show (February 2025), cementing his status as the biggest hip-hop artist. Strategic significance for India: American music industry awards shape global culture. For India: (1) Youth cultural influence — Indian youth (Gen Z, ~400M strong) consume hip-hop music; Kendrick's success validates hip-hop as a dominant global music genre, (2) Music industry growth — India's music streaming (YouTube, Spotify, etc.) now features Indian hip-hop artists (Divine, Raftaar, Badshah) inspired by Kendrick; Indian hip-hop culture is rapidly growing, (3) Soft power — Kendrick Lamar represents African-American creative excellence; his recognition by Grammy Academy (world's most prestigious music awards) validates diversity in global culture — supporting India's advocacy for representation in international forums, (4) Artist diplomacy — Kendrick's Super Bowl halftime show (watched by 100M+ globally) showcases American cultural soft power; India's film/music industry targets similar global reach (Bollywood aspires to 'Kendrick-level' global influence). For India's cultural industries, Kendrick's Grammy dominance demonstrates the global market power of authentic artistic expression and cultural grounding — relevant as India develops its music/entertainment exports.

question_text: The film 'Anora' swept the Oscars 2025. Who directed this film?
explanation: 'Anora' directed by Sean Baker swept the 97th Academy Awards (Oscars 2025, March 2, 2025) — winning Best Picture, Best Director (Sean Baker), Best Actress (Mikey Madison), and 7 nominations total. The film tells the story of a young sex worker who marries the son of a wealthy Russian oligarch, exploring themes of class, identity, and resilience. Sean Baker, known for indie-realist filmmaking ('Tangerine' 2015, 'The Florida Project' 2017), achieved mainstream critical acclaim with 'Anora.' The film's success also validates working-class narratives and New York street culture on Hollywood's biggest stage. Strategic significance for India: Oscar awards shape global cinema perceptions. For India: (1) Cinema diversity — 'Anora's' Oscar success (beating conventional prestige films) validates diverse storytelling; Indian cinema (Bollywood, regional films) aspires toward Oscar recognition; Indian directors (S.S. Rajamouli, Payal Kapadia) have received Oscar nominations (RRR Best Original Song 2023, All We Imagine as Light Best International Feature 2025 shortlist), (2) Film financing — 'Anora's' indie-production success (modest budget, huge returns) validates independent film models — relevant as Indian film industry increasingly funds regional language films, (3) Women in cinema — Mikey Madison's Best Actress win validates female-centered narratives; Indian cinema faces gender representation gaps; international validation encourages Indian productions to center female protagonists (Deepika Padukone, Vidya Balan vehicles), (4) Global competition — Indian cinema competes for international prestige; understanding what wins Oscars (character depth, social relevance, cinematic innovation) informs Indian filmmaking strategy. For India's soft power, every Indian Oscar nomination/win elevates India's cultural standing. 2025 saw Indian film Payal Kapadia's 'All We Imagine as Light' (Malayalam cinema) nominated for Best International Feature — demonstrating Indian cinema's arrival on Hollywood's radar.

question_text: Which of the following 2025 world leaders is CORRECTLY matched with their role?
explanation: Correct: Sanae Takaichi = Japan's 104th PM (first female, sworn in October 21, 2025) ✓. Incorrect: (A) Mark Carney = Canada's PM (March 14, 2025), not UK; UK PM is Keir Starmer (since July 2024), (B) Friedrich Merz = Germany's Chancellor (elected Feb 23, 2025), not French President; French President is Emmanuel Macron (since 2017), (C) Péter Magyar = Hungary's PM (April 12, 2026), not Czech PM; Czech PM is Petr Fiala (since Dec 2021). This question tests knowledge of 2025-26 leadership transitions across major democracies. Strategic note: Takaichi's appointment as Japan's first female PM was historically significant, occurring amid Japan's demographic challenges (declining workforce, aging population). Her defense-focused policies (Japan's defense budget increase to 3% GDP) signal Japan's shift toward regional security leadership amid US-China competition. For India's QUAD partnerships, Takaichi's hawkish stance on China strengthens India-Japan defense cooperation and QUAD coordination.

question_text: Pope Leo XIV (Robert Prevost) is historically significant as:
option_b: First American Pope and first Pope from the Order of Augustine
option_c: First Pope from a Protestant country
explanation: Pope Leo XIV (Robert Prevost, born Chicago 1952) is historically significant as: (1) First American Pope ever in Church history (elected May 8, 2025) — surpassing all 265 previous popes, (2) First Pope from the Augustinian order (Order of Saint Augustine) — most popes are from Jesuit or Dominican orders. He was elected 4 days after Pope Francis died (April 21, 2025). He chose 'Leo XIV' deliberately, referencing Pope Leo XIII (1878-1903) known for groundbreaking social justice encyclicals ('Rerum Novarum' on labor rights). Pope Leo XIV's multilingual abilities (English, Spanish, Italian, French) and missionary background (Peru) position him to engage Global South constituencies effectively. Strategic significance for India: An American pope represents Vatican's geopolitical recalibration. For India: (1) Vatican-US relations — An American pope may tilt Vatican foreign policy more favorably toward US interests than Pope Francis (who maintained independence), affecting Vatican's stances on China, Russia, Middle East, (2) India-Vatican ties — India has 19M+ Catholics; Leo XIV's pastoral style (emphasizing social justice, seen in Peru missionary work) could align with India's development priorities and poverty alleviation focus, (3) Religious dialogue — Leo XIV's openness to interfaith dialogue (demonstrated through Peru work with indigenous Catholics) could strengthen India-Vatican cooperation on Hindu-Christian-Sikh dialogue and minority protection. For India's diplomacy, monitoring Leo XIV's early papal decisions on geopolitical issues (Middle East wars, China relations, India-Pakistan tensions) is important for recalibrating India's Vatican engagement strategy.

question_text: BRICS admitted Indonesia (January 2025) and 10 partner countries (July 2025). Which Nobel Prize winner (Peace 2025) is from a country that is a BRICS full member?
option_d: None of the above — their countries are not BRICS members
explanation: None of the options match correctly: (A) László Krasznahorkai (Hungary) — Hungary is NOT a BRICS member (neither full nor partner as of 2025), (B) María Corina Machado (Venezuela) — Venezuela is NOT a BRICS full member (was a MERCOSUR associate, suspended from MERCOSUR 2016 over democratic backsliding; Venezuela applied for BRICS but not admitted), (C) Joel Mokyr (USA) — USA is NOT a BRICS member (BRICS was founded partly as an alternative to US-led order; BRICS explicitly rejects Western hegemony), (D) CORRECT. The 11 BRICS full members as of 2025 are: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia. Strategic note: BRICS expansion in 2025 (Indonesia entry, 10 partner countries announced) represents a significant geopolitical shift toward multipolarity and Global South assertiveness. For India: BRICS expansion validates India's 'Act South' strategy alongside 'Act East'; India chairs BRICS 2025-26 and uses this platform to amplify Global South voices on climate finance, UN reform, and alternative financial systems (de-dollarization). None of the 2025 Nobel laureates come from BRICS full member nations, illustrating BRICS's diversity beyond Nobel Prize recognition — validating BRICS's legitimacy on broader development/sovereignty grounds rather than just scientific achievement metrics (which favor Western institutions).

question_text: Match the 2025 Nobel Prize winners with correct nationalities: Nobel Peace Prize (María Corina Machado) vs. Nobel Literature (László Krasznahorkai) — which statement is CORRECT?
option_a: Machado is Venezuelan; Krasznahorkai is Romanian
option_b: Machado is Venezuelan; Krasznahorkai is Hungarian
option_c: Machado is Colombian; Krasznahorkai is Czech
option_d: Machado is Brazilian; Krasznahorkai is Polish
explanation: Nobel Peace Prize 2025: María Corina Machado — Venezuelan opposition leader, democratic rights activist (fought Maduro's dictatorship). Nobel Prize in Literature 2025: László Krasznahorkai — Hungarian author (first Hungarian to win; cited for 'compelling and visionary oeuvre'). Other 2025 Nobel laureates and nationalities: Nobel Physiology or Medicine: Mary Brunkow (USA), Fred Ramsdell (USA), Shimon Sakaguchi (Japan) — for immune tolerance discoveries. Nobel Physics: John Clarke (USA), Michel Devoret (USA), John Martinis (USA) — for macroscopic quantum effects. Nobel Chemistry: Susumu Kitagawa (Japan), Richard Robson (Australia), Omar Yaghi (USA) — for metal-organic frameworks. Nobel Economics: Joel Mokyr (USA), Philippe Aghion (France/UK-based), Peter Howitt (USA) — for innovation and growth. Strategic note: 2025 Nobel laureates reflect Western-centric scientific achievement recognition (9 out of 17 laureates from USA), while Peace Prize goes to a Global South democracy activist. This asymmetry validates India's advocacy for reforming international recognition mechanisms to better represent Global South scientific contributions — a key part of India's G20 and UN leadership agendas.

question_text: Which summit-related statement from 2025 is CORRECT?
option_a: COP30 raised climate finance target to $300B/year by 2035
option_b: G7 Kananaskis produced a joint communiqué signed by all 7 leaders
option_c: ASEAN KL 2025 admitted Timor-Leste as its 11th member
option_d: SCO 2025 was held in Astana, Kazakhstan
explanation: ASEAN KL (Kuala Lumpur) Summit, October 2025 admitted Timor-Leste as its 11th full member — ASEAN's first expansion since Cambodia joined in 1999 (26-year gap). Incorrect: (A) COP30 (Belém, Brazil, November 2025) raised climate finance to $1.3 TRILLION/year by 2035 (vs developed nations' initial $300B offer), not $300B; (B) G7 Kananaskis (June 2025, Canada) had NO joint communiqué signed by all 7 — Trump left early, and the remaining 6 members issued a joint statement without full G7 consensus; (C) CORRECT ✓; (D) SCO Summit 2025 was held in Tianjin, China (October 2025, Modi's first mainland China visit in 7 years), NOT Astana (which hosted SCO 2024). Strategic significance: These summits reflect major 2025 geopolitical developments. For India: (1) COP30's $1.3T climate finance raises hopes for India's climate action funding (India needs $2.5T+ by 2070 for net-zero transition), (2) G7's dysfunction (Trump's absence) validating India's BRICS positioning as an alternative bloc, (3) ASEAN expansion (Timor-Leste) strengthens India-ASEAN ties and QUAD positioning in Indo-Pacific, (4) SCO meeting in China demonstrates India-China normalization and geopolitical maneuvering amid US competition. These summits collectively show 2025 as a year of institutional realignment toward multipolarity.

question_text: Which country's university (ETH Zürich) published an assessment on India's air superiority in Operation Sindoor 2025?
explanation: ETH Zürich (Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule Zürich / Swiss Federal Institute of Technology) is in Zurich, Switzerland. Its Center for Security Studies (CSS) published detailed technical analysis on India's air superiority tactics and precision strike capabilities demonstrated in Operation Sindoor (May 7, 2025) against terrorist camps in Pakistan/PoK. ETH Zürich is consistently ranked among the world's top universities (along with MIT, Cambridge, Oxford, Stanford). Notable alumni: Albert Einstein (1896-1900), 21 Nobel Prize winners. Strategic significance for India: International academic recognition of India's military capabilities enhances India's strategic credibility. For India: (1) CSS analysis validated Operation Sindoor's technical success — India's precision targeting of 9 camps, rapid execution (16 days from Pahalgam attack to strikes), and ceasefire restraint demonstrated modern air power management, (2) Geopolitical messaging — ETH Zürich's neutral, scholarly assessment (vs. geopolitical think-tanks with bias) carries weight in international policy circles; India's demonstration of capability influences QUAD allies' confidence in India's defense readiness, (3) Technology expertise — ETH Zürich's engineering faculty (robotics, AI, aerospace) increasingly collaborates with India on dual-use technologies relevant to defense (TUSAS-India drone partnerships, satellite systems), (4) Soft power — Switzerland's neutrality and academic prestige lend credibility; when Swiss institutions publish India-positive assessments, it validates India's narratives in international media. For India's military modernization, Operation Sindoor and its international analysis demonstrate the value of precision strike capabilities as deterrents against terrorism — influencing India's defense budgeting priorities and QUAD coordination on drone/AI technologies.

question_text: The India-UK FTA (CETA 2025) will come into force in May 2026. What is the current bilateral trade value between India and UK?
explanation: India-UK bilateral trade (2025): $56 billion comprising India exports (~$30B: textiles, pharmaceuticals, IT services, engineering goods, diamonds) and UK exports (~$26B: whisky, aerospace products, machinery, organic chemicals, medical devices). CETA (signed July 24, 2025) aims to double bilateral trade to $112 billion by 2030 (projected 100% increase over 5 years = 15-20%/year growth rate). Projected $34 billion/year additional trade flows from 2040. Strategic significance for India: CETA represents India-UK's post-Brexit recalibration. For India: (1) UK market access — 99% of Indian exports face zero tariffs under CETA (textiles, pharmaceuticals, IT services, engineering); this removes non-tariff barriers that previously protected UK industries, (2) Industrial cooperation — 90% of UK exports to India get reduced tariffs; this includes aerospace (defense partnerships with HAL, Tata), machinery (manufacturing collaborations), creating deep bilateral industrial ties, (3) Trade diversification — CETA diversifies India's EU trade away from high-tariff EU nations (France, Germany) toward post-Brexit UK focused on flexibility. For India's economic strategy, doubling UK trade by 2030 aligns with India's target of $500B+ US-India trade (Modi-Trump COMPACT) and sustained EU trade expansion. The CETA agreement also includes IP protection, digital commerce, labor standards — modernizing India-UK partnership beyond colonial-era trade dynamics.

question_text: In the context of Iran's nuclear program, uranium enriched to what percentage purity is considered 'near weapons-grade'?
explanation: Weapons-grade uranium = 90%+ U-235 enrichment (technically <5% purity is Low Enriched Uranium — LEU for power reactors, 5-20% is Intermediate, 20-90% is Highly Enriched Uranium — HEU for research reactors, 90%+ is weapons-usable). Iran had enriched uranium to 60% U-235 purity by March 2025 — approaching but below weapons-grade threshold, hence termed 'near weapons-grade.' The JCPOA (Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, 2015) had capped Iran's enrichment at 3.67% U-235 purity. After Trump withdrew from JCPOA (May 2018), Iran gradually resumed enrichment, reaching 60% by early 2025. The IAEA Board resolution (June 12, 2025) declared Iran non-compliant with IAEA safeguards (70% of declared nuclear material was diverted to undeclared sites). This resolution triggered the Twelve-Day War (June 13-24, 2025). Strategic significance for India: Iran's nuclear escalation affects India's energy security and Middle East regional stability. For India: (1) Oil supplies — Iran's escalation triggered military conflict; India's oil imports from Iran halted during the war, disrupting energy supplies and driving global oil prices up 40%+, (2) Nuclear proliferation — If Iran achieves weapons capability, Middle East nuclear arms race accelerates (Saudi Arabia, UAE also pursue nuclear programs); this destabilizes the region and threatens India's energy suppliers, (3) Geopolitical leverage — A nuclear-armed Iran increases Iran's regional assertiveness and reduces India's ability to balance Iran-Saudi dynamics. For India's strategic autonomy, diversifying energy sources (Russia, Saudi, UAE, Iraq, US shale) reduces Iran dependency — a lesson India learned painfully in 2026 when Iran-related conflicts disrupted supplies multiple times.

question_text: The Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) — which India has not joined — was signed in 2018 without the USA. Which country chairs CPTPP in 2025?
explanation: Japan chairs CPTPP in 2025. CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, signed November 2018) comprises 12 members: Japan, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, Mexico, Peru, Chile, and UK (joined 2023 as 12th member). CPTPP was originally the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) negotiated under Obama, but Trump withdrew the USA on January 23, 2017; the remaining 11 nations renegotiated and signed CPTPP in 2018. Strategic significance for India: CPTPP's evolution without USA and India represents a critical geopolitical gap for India's Indo-Pacific strategy. For India: (1) Trade exclusion — India has NOT joined CPTPP; CPTPP members (especially ASEAN members Vietnam, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei) offer preferential tariffs only to CPTPP members, disadvantaging Indian exports, (2) India-CPTPP gap — India's trade with CPTPP members (~$150B) would grow if India joined, but CPTPP requires high labor/environmental standards, IP protection, and investment provisions that constrain India's policy space, (3) China's move — China applied for CPTPP membership (2021); if China joins, it gains preferential access to Pacific markets and strengthens China's economic influence in Asia-Pacific, reducing India's leverage, (4) India's alternatives — India pursues bilateral FTAs (India-UK CETA 2025, India-Australia FTA 2022, India-ASEAN trade expansion) and RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, joined 2022) as substitutes for CPTPP membership. For India's Indo-Pacific strategy, CPTPP's expansion without India represents a gap in India's regional trade architecture — validating India's efforts to deepen ASEAN ties and pursue alternative trade partnerships. Japan's CPTPP chairmanship (2025) aligns with Japan's QUAD partnership with India; India-Japan coordination on Indo-Pacific architecture is stronger through bilateral channels than CPTPP mechanisms.

question_text: Which of the following is CORRECTLY matched — an Indian government scheme/initiative with its purpose?
option_a: MAITRI → Maritime training initiative for Indo-Pacific (QUAD)
option_d: Sagar Bandhu → India's deep-sea mining program
explanation: MAITRI (Maritime Initiative for Awareness, Training and Cooperation for the Indian Ocean) is a QUAD initiative co-led by India and Australia to train Indo-Pacific Coast Guard personnel in disaster response, search-and-rescue, maritime security cooperation. MAITRI exemplifies India's QUAD role as a security provider in Indo-Pacific. Incorrect: (B) BHISHM = Bike-mounted Hospital System (portable field hospital gifted to Maldives — medical diplomacy, not surveillance), (C) LeadIT = India-SWEDEN (NOT India-USA) partnership for heavy industry decarbonization, (D) Sagar Bandhu = India's humanitarian/disaster relief operation to assist Sri Lanka during Cyclone Ditwah (November 2025), not a deep-sea mining program. Strategic note: These initiatives reflect India's multi-domain engagement in Indo-Pacific — maritime security (MAITRI), health diplomacy (BHISHM), climate transition (LeadIT), and humanitarian leadership (Sagar Bandhu). For India's regional positioning, these initiatives collectively demonstrate India as a 'First Responder' and 'First Partner' in the Indian Ocean and Indo-Pacific.

question_text: South Korea held a snap presidential election on June 3, 2025. Who was the new President-elect who defeated the conservative candidate?
explanation: Lee Jae-myung (Democratic Party, centrist-progressive) won South Korea's June 3, 2025 snap presidential election with 50.7% of vote, defeating conservative candidate Han Duck-soo (31.4%). Lee had previously narrowly lost the 2022 presidential election to Yoon Suk-yeol (Conservative party). Lee became President following Yoon Suk-yeol's Constitutional Court impeachment removal on April 4, 2025 (triggered by Yoon's illegal December 3, 2024 martial law declaration). Lee also hosted APEC 2025 Summit in Gyeongju, South Korea (November 2025). Strategic significance for India: South Korea's political transition affects QUAD dynamics and Indo-Pacific strategy.
